items.title: Self-adjointness and the flow of a self-adjoint operator perturbed by a bounded operator commuting with its flow
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint
operator on $H$ with domain $D(A)$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and let $B$ be a
bounded self-adjoint operator on $H$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) with
$$B\,e^{isA}=e^{isA}B\qquad(s\in\mathbb R),$$
where $e^{isA}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{is\lambda}\,dE_A(\lambda)$ is the unitary
group of $A$ in the spectral calculus
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Put $A+B$ on its natural domain
$D(A+B):=D(A)\cap D(B)=D(A)$. Then:

(a) $A+B$ is self-adjoint;

(b) $e^{isB}e^{itA}=e^{itA}e^{isB}$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$; the flows of
$A$ and of the bounded $B$ commute;

(c) the family $s\mapsto P(s):=e^{isA}e^{isB}$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group
([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]), and its
infinitesimal generator $G$
([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]) is $G=i(A+B)$: the
quotient $\frac1s\bigl(P(s)x-x\bigr)$ converges as $s\to0$ exactly for
$x\in D(A)$, with limit $i(A+B)x$. Consequently $P(s)=e^{is(A+B)}$ for every
$s\in\mathbb R$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; a nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$; a self-adjoint operator $A$; a bounded self-adjoint
operator $B$ commuting with every $e^{isA}$; real $s,t,\lambda$; a unit vector
or vector $x$.

[F1] **Flow calculus.** For a self-adjoint $T$ with spectral
projection-valued measure $E_T$ and $U_T(s):=e^{isT}$: $U_T$ is a strongly
continuous one-parameter unitary group with $U_T(s)^{*}=U_T(-s)$,
$U_T(s)D(T)=D(T)$ and $TU_T(s)=U_T(s)T$ on $D(T)$; the quotient
$\frac1s(U_T(s)x-x)$ converges as $s\to0$ exactly for $x\in D(T)$, with limit
$iTx$; and for every bounded Borel $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ one has
$\|f(T)\|\le\sup|f|$ and $f(T)U_T(s)=U_T(s)f(T)$, where
$f(T)=\int f\,dE_T$
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]).

[F2] **Resolvents.** For $\lambda\ne0$ the operator $A+i\lambda$ maps $D(A)$
bijectively onto $H$, and its inverse $(A+i\lambda)^{-1}=\int(\mu+i\lambda)^{-1}dE_A(\mu)$
is bounded with norm at most $1/|\lambda|$, by [F1] applied to
$f(\mu)=(\mu+i\lambda)^{-1}$ (whose supremum is $1/|\lambda|$) together with
the calculus identity $(A+i\lambda)(A+i\lambda)^{-1}=I$
([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]).

[F3] **Neumann series.** If $R\in\mathcal B(H)$ with $\|R\|<1$, then $I-R$ is
invertible and $(I-R)^{-1}=\sum_{n\ge0}R^n$ in operator norm
([[lem-neumann-series-and-small-perturbations-of-bounded-inverses]] clause 1,
[[def-operator-norm]]).

[F4] **Stone uniqueness.** Two strongly continuous one-parameter unitary
groups with the same infinitesimal generator agree at every time; equivalently
$s\mapsto e^{isT}$ is determined by the self-adjoint $T$
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]],
[[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; prove self-adjointness of $A+B$ by the Neumann
series for the resolvent of $A$, differentiate the conjugation curve to obtain
the commutation of the two flows, and identify the generator of the product
group by comparing difference quotients, concluding with Stone's theorem.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Symmetry and domain of $A+B$] The domain $D(A+B)=D(A)$ is a dense linear subspace of $H$ because $D(A)$ is dense and $B$ is everywhere defined and linear; for $x,y\in D(A)$, using that $A$ is symmetric and $B$ is self-adjoint and bounded, $\langle(A+B)x,y\rangle=\langle Ax,y\rangle+\langle Bx,y\rangle=\langle x,Ay\rangle+\langle x,By\rangle=\langle x,(A+B)y\rangle$, so $A+B$ is densely defined and symmetric. [given, algebra]

1.2 [Surjectivity of $(A+B)\pm i\lambda$] Fix $\lambda>\|B\|$ (if $B=0$ take $\lambda=1$); by [F2] the map $(A+i\lambda):D(A)\to H$ is a bijection with inverse of norm at most $1/\lambda$, so $(A+i\lambda)^{-1}B$ is bounded with $\|(A+i\lambda)^{-1}B\|\le\|B\|/\lambda<1$ by submultiplicativity of the operator norm and [F3] makes $I+(A+i\lambda)^{-1}B$ invertible on $H$ with bounded inverse; for $x\in D(A)$ one has $(A+i\lambda)^{-1}Bx\in D(A)$, hence $(A+B+i\lambda)x=(A+i\lambda)\bigl(I+(A+i\lambda)^{-1}B\bigr)x$ and, since $I+(A+i\lambda)^{-1}B$ maps $D(A)$ onto $D(A)$ and $(A+i\lambda)$ maps $D(A)$ onto $H$, the operator $(A+B)+i\lambda$ maps $D(A)$ onto $H$, and the same argument with $-\lambda$ shows that $(A+B)-i\lambda$ maps $D(A)$ onto $H$. [F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 [Adjoint inclusion] Let $y\in D((A+B)^{*})$ and put $z:=(A+B)^{*}y$; for every $x\in D(A)$ one has $\langle Ax,y\rangle+\langle Bx,y\rangle=\langle x,z\rangle$, that is $\langle Ax,y\rangle=\langle x,z-By\rangle$ because $B^{*}=B$ and $By\in H$, and since $A$ is self-adjoint the existence of the vector $z-By$ representing $x\mapsto\langle Ax,y\rangle$ forces $y\in D(A)$ with $Ay=z-By$, so $D((A+B)^{*})\subseteq D(A)=D(A+B)$ with $(A+B)^{*}y=(A+B)y$ there. [F1, given, algebra]

1.4 [Commutation of the flows] Fix $t$ and $x\in H$ and define $g(s):=e^{isB}e^{itA}e^{-isB}x$; by [F1] applied to the self-adjoint operator $B$ (whose domain is all of $H$) the difference quotients $\frac1h(e^{i(s+h)B}y-e^{isB}y)\to iBe^{isB}y$ and $\frac1h(e^{-i(s+h)B}y-e^{-isB}y)\to-ie^{-isB}By$ for every $y$, so the product rule gives $g'(s)=e^{isB}\bigl(iBe^{itA}-ie^{itA}B\bigr)e^{-isB}x$, and the hypothesis $Be^{itA}=e^{itA}B$ makes this derivative vanish for every $s$; hence $g$ is constant with value $g(0)=e^{itA}x$, that is $e^{isB}e^{itA}=e^{itA}e^{isB}$ for all $s,t$, which is the first identity of (b). [F1, given, algebra]

1.5 [Quotient of the product group on $D(A)$] Put $P(s):=e^{isA}e^{isB}$ and let $x\in D(A)$; the algebraic identity $\frac1s(P(s)x-x)=e^{isA}\frac1s(e^{isB}x-x)+\frac1s(e^{isA}x-x)$ holds for every $s\ne0$, and as $s\to0$ the first term converges to $iBx$ because $\frac1s(e^{isB}x-x)\to iBx$ in norm by [F1] and $e^{isA}\to I$ strongly, while the second converges to $iAx$ by [F1]; hence the quotient of $P$ at $x$ converges, with limit $i(A+B)x$. [F1, algebra]

2.1 [Self-adjointness] Step 1.1 gives $A+B\subseteq(A+B)^{*}$ and step 1.3 gives $(A+B)^{*}\subseteq A+B$ including domains, so $A+B=(A+B)^{*}$, which is (a). [step 1.1, step 1.3]

2.2 [Group property and strong continuity] By step 1.4, $P(s)P(t)=e^{isA}e^{isB}e^{itA}e^{itB}=e^{isA}e^{itA}e^{isB}e^{itB}=P(s+t)$ and $P(s)^{*}=e^{-isB}e^{-isA}=e^{-isA}e^{-isB}=P(-s)$; each factor is strongly continuous, and the estimate $\|P(s)x-P(s_0)x\|\le\|e^{isA}(e^{isB}x-e^{is_0B}x)\|+\|(e^{isA}-e^{is_0A})e^{is_0B}x\|$ shows that $P$ is strongly continuous, hence a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group. [step 1.4, F1, algebra]

2.3 [No larger domain] Let $x\in H$ and suppose that $\frac1s(P(s)x-x)$ converges, to $y\in H$; by step 1.4, $P(s)=e^{isB}e^{isA}$, so $e^{isA}x=e^{-isB}P(s)x$ and the identity $\frac1s(e^{isA}x-x)=e^{-isB}\frac1s(P(s)x-x)+\frac1s(e^{-isB}x-x)$ holds; the first term converges to $y$ because $e^{-isB}\to I$ strongly and $\frac1s(P(s)x-x)\to y$, and the second converges to $-iBx$ by [F1] applied to the self-adjoint operator $-B$, so $\frac1s(e^{isA}x-x)$ converges and [F1] gives $x\in D(A)$ with $y=i(A+B)x$. [step 1.4, F1, algebra]

3.1 [Generator identification] By step 2.2 the family $P$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with infinitesimal generator $G$; steps 1.5 and 2.3 show that the quotient of $P$ at $x$ converges exactly for $x\in D(A)$, with limit $i(A+B)x$; hence $D(G)=D(A)$ and $G=i(A+B)$, which is the generator statement of (c). [step 1.5, step 2.2, step 2.3]

4.1 [Identification of the groups] By [F1] the family $s\mapsto e^{is(A+B)}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose quotient at $x$ converges exactly for $x\in D(A+B)=D(A)$, to $i(A+B)x$; by step 3.1 it has the same infinitesimal generator $i(A+B)$ as $P$, so Stone's theorem [F4] yields $P(s)=e^{is(A+B)}$ for every $s$, completing (c); (b) is step 1.4. [step 1.4, step 3.1, F1, F4] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the hypothesis is a commutation with the flow.** The hypothesis
  $Be^{isA}=e^{isA}B$ for all $s$ is a commutation of the bounded operator
  with every element of the unitary group of $A$; it implies, but is not
  assumed as, a formal commutator identity on a small domain, and it is the
  exact form in which the model's internal matrices commute with the free
  flow.
- **Bounded perturbation.** Clause (a) is the standard self-adjointness of a
  self-adjoint operator perturbed by a bounded self-adjoint operator; the flow
  hypothesis is not needed for it, only for the product formula of (b) and the
  generator statement of (c).

items.title: The SU(2) lift of the spatial rotation action on the component-valued wave-function space and its coordinate generators
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put
$r:=2s+1$, and let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with inner product linear in the
first argument
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]). Let $SO(3)$ be the
special orthogonal group ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]), let
$U(R)$ for $R\in SO(3)$ be the componentwise spatial rotation action
$$(U(R)f)_{l}(x):=f_{l}(R^{-1}x)\qquad(l=1,\dots,r)$$
of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], and let
$\rho:SU(2)\to SO(3)$, $\rho(q)(v)=qvq^{-1}$, be the covering homomorphism of
[[ex-su-two-to-so-three-as-a-covering-homomorphism]] (with $SU(2)$ identified
with the unit quaternions as in [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]],
so that $\rho$ is smooth by
[[def-covering-homomorphism-of-lie-groups]]). Let
$F_{s}:\mathcal S_{2s}\to V_{s}=\mathbb C^{r}$ be the unitary identification
$v_{k}\mapsto e_{s-k}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]] clause
(d) (for $s=0$, $\mathcal S_{0}=\mathbb C v_{0}$ and $F_{0}v_{0}:=1$),
define $D_{s}:SU(2)\to U(V_{s})$ by
$D_{s}(W):=F_{s}U_{2s}(W)F_{s}^{-1}$ for $s>0$ and
$D_{0}(W):=I_{\mathbb C}$, and let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the self-adjoint
spin endomorphisms of $V_{s}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (a). By clauses
(b),(d),(f) of the theorem the maps $D_{s}$ are strongly continuous unitary
representations of $SU(2)$.
For $W\in SU(2)$ define the matrix action $M_{s}(W)\in\mathcal B(H_{s})$ and
the lifted operator $U_{s}(W)$ by
$$(M_{s}(W)f)(x):=D_{s}(W)\bigl(f(x)\bigr),\qquad U_{s}(W):=U(\rho(W))\,M_{s}(W)\qquad(f\in H_{s},\ x\in\mathbb R^{3}),$$
where the matrix $D_{s}(W)$ acts on the column vector $f(x)\in\mathbb C^{r}$.
Finally let $R_{i}(t)$, $i=1,2,3$, be the coordinate rotation matrices and
$L_{i}$ the self-adjoint coordinate-rotation generators on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] (so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$), and put
$A_{i}(t):=\cos(t/2)I_{2}-i\sin(t/2)\sigma_{i}\in SU(2)$ with the Pauli
matrices $\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e). Then:

(a) for every $W\in SU(2)$ the operator $U_{s}(W)$ is unitary, with
$U_{s}(I)=\mathrm{id}$ and $U_{s}(W_{1}W_{2})=U_{s}(W_{1})U_{s}(W_{2})$ for
all $W_{1},W_{2}\in SU(2)$, and $W\mapsto U_{s}(W)$ is strongly continuous
([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]);

(b) $\rho(A_{i}(t))=R_{i}(t)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$ and every $i$, and
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary
group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]);

(c) the operators $L_{i}$ and $S_{i}$ strongly commute (their spectral
projection-valued measures commute;
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]), the sum $J_{i}:=L_{i}+S_{i}$ with
domain $D(J_{i}):=D(L_{i})$ is self-adjoint, and
$$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
moreover for $W\in SU(2)$ one has the conjugation identities including
domains
$$U_{s}(W)Q_{j}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lj}Q_{l},\qquad U_{s}(W)P_{k}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lk}P_{l},$$
where $Q_{j},P_{k}$ are the componentwise position and momentum operators of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a) and
$\rho(W)_{lj}$ are the matrix entries of $\rho(W)$ in the standard basis;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is a mathematical statement about the
finite-dimensional spin representation and the componentwise rotation action;
it asserts no physical interpretation, no measurement, no dynamics and no
value of $\hbar$, $s$ or $W$. The spatial action enters only through
$U(R)=U(\rho(W))$ and the internal action only through $M_{s}(W)$; no action
on a second spatial or internal factor is introduced.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the spin
label $s$, $r=2s+1$, the space $H_{s}$; the rotation action $U(R)$ and the
covering homomorphism $\rho$; the identification $F_{s}$ and the
representation $D_{s}=F_{s}U_{2s}F_{s}^{-1}$ with spin operators
$S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$; the operators $M_{s}(W)$ and $U_{s}(W)$; the coordinate
rotations $R_{i}(t)$, $A_{i}(t)$ and the generators $L_{i}$; $W,W_{1},W_{2}\in
SU(2)$, real $s_{0},t$ (use $u$ for the group parameter where it is not the
spin label).

[F1] **The covering.** $\rho:SU(2)\to SO(3)$, $\rho(q)(v)=qvq^{-1}$ on
imaginary quaternions, is a surjective two-sheeted covering homomorphism of
Lie groups with kernel $\{1,-1\}$, hence in particular a smooth, continuous,
multiplicative map onto $SO(3)$; and for every $q\in SU(2)$ and $v\in\mathbb
R^{3}$ identified with an imaginary quaternion, $\rho(q)v=qvq^{-1}$
([[ex-su-two-to-so-three-as-a-covering-homomorphism]],
[[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]],
[[def-covering-homomorphism-of-lie-groups]], [[def-quaternions]]).

[F2] **Spatial rotation action.** $U(R)$ is a unitary operator for every $R$
with $U(I)=\mathrm{id}$, $U(RS)=U(R)U(S)$ and $U(R)^{-1}=U(R^{-1})$; the map
$R\mapsto U(R)$ is strongly continuous on $SO(3)$; and
$U(R)D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$, $U(R)Q_{j}U(R)^{-1}=\sum_{l}R_{lj}Q_{l}$,
$U(R)D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$, $U(R)P_{k}U(R)^{-1}=\sum_{l}R_{lk}P_{l}$ as
operator identities including domains
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F3] **Coordinate rotation generators.** For each $i$, $U_{i}(t):=U(R_{i}(t))$
is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with
$U_{i}(t)=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ for the self-adjoint generator $L_{i}$, and for
$\psi\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$ one has
$L_{i}\psi=-i\hbar\sum_{j}(e_{i}\times x)_{j}D_{j}\psi
=\sum_{j,k}\varepsilon_{ijk}Q_{j}P_{k}\psi$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clauses
(a),(b), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]).

[F4] **Internal representation.** For $s>0$, $n=2s$ and
$F_{s}:\mathcal S_{n}\to V_{s}$ the unitary identification $v_{k}\mapsto
e_{s-k}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]] clause (d),
$D_{s}(W)=F_{s}U_{n}(W)F_{s}^{-1}$ with $U_{n}(W)=W^{\otimes n}|_{\mathcal
S_{n}}$ defines a group homomorphism $SU(2)\to U(V_{s})$ that is continuous
in operator norm; for $s=0$, $D_{0}(W)=I_{\mathbb C}$; and $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$
are the self-adjoint matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] with
$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k}$ and
$S^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]]
clauses (b),(c),(d),(f),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c)).

[F5] **Internal coordinate generator.** For every $i$ the curve
$t\mapsto A_{i}(t)$ lies in $SU(2)$, satisfies $A_{i}(s_{0})A_{i}(t)=A_{i}(s_{0}+t)$
and $A_{i}(0)=I_{2}$, and the family $t\mapsto D_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ has
infinitesimal generator $-iJ_{i}$: for every $v\in V_{s}$,
$\frac1t\bigl(D_{s}(A_{i}(t))v-v\bigr)\to-iJ_{i}v$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]]
clauses (d),(e), [[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]],
[[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]],
[[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

[F6] **Matrix actions commute with componentwise operators.** For
$W\in SU(2)$ the map $M_{s}(W)$ is linear and isometric, hence unitary on
$H_{s}$ (the values $D_{s}(W)$ are unitary matrices), and it commutes with the
componentwise operators $U(R)$, $Q_{j}$, $P_{k}$ and with every componentwise
multiplication operator: for $f$ in the relevant domain,
$M_{s}(W)U(R)f=U(R)M_{s}(W)f$, $M_{s}(W)Q_{j}f=Q_{j}M_{s}(W)f$ and
$M_{s}(W)P_{k}f=P_{k}M_{s}(W)f$, with $M_{s}(W)$ preserving each of the
domains; this is checked componentwise from the definitions
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a),
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]).

[F7] **Commutation with a flow.** If a bounded $S\in\mathcal B(H)$ commutes
with every element $e^{iuT}$ of the flow of a self-adjoint $T$, then $S$
commutes with every spectral projection $E_{T}(\Lambda)$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-unitary-conjugation-and-commutation-calculus]]
clause (c)).

[F8] **Calculus of a strongly commuting pair.** If the self-adjoint operators
$A$ and $B$ have commuting spectral projection-valued measures, then
$f(B)g(A)=g(A)f(B)$ for all bounded Borel $f,g$
([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-bounded-borel-calculus-of-commuting-operators]]
clause (a), [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b)).

[F9] **Product flow.** If $A$ is self-adjoint and $B$ is bounded self-adjoint
with $Be^{iuA}=e^{iuA}B$ for all real $u$, then $A+B$ with domain $D(A)$ is
self-adjoint and $e^{iu(A+B)}=e^{iuA}e^{iuB}$ for all $u$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clauses (a),(c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; verify unitarity and multiplicativity from the
matrix action, compute the quaternion image of the coordinate subgroups,
transport the commutation of the internal matrices with the spatial flow into
strong spectral commutation, and identify the coordinate generators through
the product-flow lemma and Stone's theorem.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F9].

1.1 [Unitary and representation law] Let $W\in SU(2)$; the fibrewise matrix action $M_{s}(W)$ is well defined on almost-everywhere classes, linear, and isometric because $\|D_{s}(W)f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}=\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}$ for almost every $x$ with $D_{s}(W)$ unitary, so $\|M_{s}(W)f\|=\|f\|$ and $M_{s}(W)$ extends to a unitary operator with inverse $M_{s}(W^{-1})$, and $M_{s}(W_{1})M_{s}(W_{2})=M_{s}(W_{1}W_{2})$ again componentwise; $U(\rho(W))$ is unitary by [F2], so $U_{s}(W)$ is unitary with $U_{s}(I)=U(I)M_{s}(I)=\mathrm{id}$. Using [F6] to move $M_{s}(W_{1})$ across $U(\rho(W_{2}))$ and the multiplicativity $\rho(W_{1}W_{2})=\rho(W_{1})\rho(W_{2})$ of [F1] together with $D_{s}(W_{1}W_{2})=D_{s}(W_{1})D_{s}(W_{2})$, one gets $U_{s}(W_{1})U_{s}(W_{2})=U(\rho(W_{1}))U(\rho(W_{2}))M_{s}(W_{1})M_{s}(W_{2})=U_{s}(W_{1}W_{2})$. [F1, F2, F4, F6, algebra]

1.2 [Coordinate rotations under $\rho$] Under the identification of $SU(2)$ with the unit quaternions, $A_{i}(t)$ corresponds to the quaternion $q=c+sr$ with $c=\cos(t/2)$, $s=\sin(t/2)$ and $r=u_{i}$, where $u_{1}=i,u_{2}=j,u_{3}=k$; writing $v=\alpha r+w$ with $\alpha=v\cdot r$ and $w=v-(\alpha)r$ perpendicular to $r$ and using the quaternion product $vw=(v\cdot w)+v\times w$ for imaginary quaternions and $r^{2}=-1$, one computes $qvq^{-1}=(c^{2}-s^{2})\alpha r+(c^{2}+s^{2})w+2cs\,(r\times w)=\alpha r+\cos t\,w+\sin t\,(r\times w)$, because $rwr=w$ for $w\perp r$ by the triple identity $(r\times w)\times r=w(r\cdot r)-r(r\cdot w)$; on the standard basis this is exactly the rotation about $u_{i}$ through the angle $t$ with the orientation of the ordered pair of the remaining two axes, so comparing with the matrices $R_{i}(t)$ of [F3] gives $\rho(A_{i}(t))=R_{i}(t)$ for every $t$ and $i$. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

1.3 [Strong commutation of the spatial generators with internal projections] Let $P$ be a spectral projection of the self-adjoint matrix $S_{i}$ and let $M$ be the bounded self-adjoint fibrewise matrix action $(Mf)(x):=Pf(x)$; by [F6] the operator $M$ commutes with $U(R_{i}(u))=e^{-iuL_{i}/\hbar}$ for every $u$, so by [F7] applied to the self-adjoint operator $L_{i}$ and the bounded $M$ one has $ME_{L_{i}}(\Lambda)=E_{L_{i}}(\Lambda)M$ for every Borel $\Lambda$; taking for $P$ every spectral projection $E_{S_{i}}(\Sigma)$ of the finite matrix $S_{i}$ gives $E_{L_{i}}(\Lambda)E_{S_{i}}(\Sigma)=E_{S_{i}}(\Sigma)E_{L_{i}}(\Lambda)$ for all Borel $\Lambda,\Sigma$, which is the strong commutation of $L_{i}$ and $S_{i}$ in the sense of [F8]. [F4, F6, F7, algebra]

1.4 [Internal coordinate generator] By [F5] the family $t\mapsto D_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on $V_{s}$ with infinitesimal generator $-iJ_{i}$; the family $t\mapsto e^{-itS_{i}/\hbar}$ is by [F4] and the spectral calculus a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose quotient at $v$ is $-iS_{i}v/\hbar=-iJ_{i}v$, so by Stone's theorem the two groups agree: $D_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itS_{i}/\hbar}$ for every $t$. [F4, F5, algebra]

1.5 [Strong continuity of the lift] Let $W_{m}\to W$ in $SU(2)$ and $f\in H_{s}$; since $\rho$ is continuous by [F1], $\rho(W_{m})\to\rho(W)$ and [F2] gives $\|U(\rho(W_{m}))g-U(\rho(W))g\|\to0$ for every fixed $g$; since $\|D_{s}(W_{m})-D_{s}(W)\|\to0$ in operator norm by [F4], $\|M_{s}(W_{m})f-M_{s}(W)f\|\le\sup_{x}\|D_{s}(W_{m})-D_{s}(W)\|\,\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}$ in $L^{2}$ norm tends to $0$; combining, $\|U_{s}(W_{m})f-U_{s}(W)f\|\le\|U(\rho(W_{m}))(M_{s}(W_{m})f-M_{s}(W)f)\|+\|U(\rho(W_{m}))M_{s}(W)f-U(\rho(W))M_{s}(W)f\|\to0$, so $W\mapsto U_{s}(W)$ is strongly continuous. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Conjugations of position and momentum] By [F6] the matrix action $M_{s}(W)$ commutes with $Q_{j}$ and preserves $D(Q_{j})$, so $U_{s}(W)Q_{j}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=U(\rho(W))Q_{j}U(\rho(W))^{-1}$, and [F2] gives $U(\rho(W))Q_{j}U(\rho(W))^{-1}=\sum_{l}\rho(W)_{lj}Q_{l}$ including domains; the same computation with $P_{k}$ and [F2] gives $U_{s}(W)P_{k}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l}\rho(W)_{lk}P_{l}$, which is the conjugation identity of (c). [step 1.1, F2, F6, algebra]

2.2 [Self-adjoint sum and product flow] By step 1.3 the spectral measures of $L_{i}$ and $S_{i}$ commute, so [F8] with $f(\mu)=e^{-i\mu t/\hbar}$, $g(\lambda)=e^{-i\lambda u/\hbar}$ gives $e^{-itS_{i}/\hbar}e^{-iuL_{i}/\hbar}=e^{-iuL_{i}/\hbar}e^{-itS_{i}/\hbar}$ for all $t,u$; hence [F9] applies with $A:=L_{i}$ and the bounded self-adjoint $B:=S_{i}$, so the sum $J_{i}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ with domain $D(L_{i})$ is self-adjoint and $e^{-itJ_{i}/\hbar}=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}e^{-itS_{i}/\hbar}$ for every $t$. [step 1.3, F4, F8, F9, algebra]

3.1 [Coordinate subgroup generator] Let $t$ be real; by step 1.2, $\rho(A_{i}(t))=R_{i}(t)$, so by [F3] and step 1.4 $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=U(R_{i}(t))M_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}e^{-itS_{i}/\hbar}=e^{-itJ_{i}/\hbar}$ by step 2.2; since the right-hand side is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group in $t$ and $A_{i}$ is multiplicative by [F5], $t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with the displayed generator, which is (b) and the generator identity of (c). [step 1.2, step 1.4, step 2.2, F3, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly] Step 1.1 proves unitarity, the identity and the representation law, and step 1.5 proves strong continuity, which is (a); step 3.1 proves (b) and the generator identity of (c); step 1.3 proves the strong commutation of $L_{i}$ and $S_{i}$, step 2.2 the self-adjointness of $J_{i}$, and step 2.1 the conjugation identities of (c); (d) records only the scope of these mathematical assertions. [step 1.1, step 1.3, step 1.5, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Kernel and the two lifts.** Since $D_{s}(-I_{2})=(-1)^{2s}I$ by the
  diagonal action and [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]]
  clauses (a),(b) (for $s=0$ also $D_{0}(-I_{2})=I$), one has
  $U_{s}(-I_{2})=(-1)^{2s}\mathrm{id}$. For half-integer $s$ this is
  $-\mathrm{id}\ne\mathrm{id}$, so $W\mapsto U_{s}(W)$ does not factor
  through $\rho$: no map $V$ with $V(\rho(W))=U_{s}(W)$ exists, since
  $\rho(-I_{2})=\rho(I_{2})=I$ would force $V(I)=-\mathrm{id}$. For integer
  $s$, $-I_{2}$ acts as the identity and the action passes to the rotation
  group $SU(2)/\{I_{2},-I_{2}\}\cong SO(3)$ of
  [[ex-su-two-to-so-three-as-a-covering-homomorphism]]. On a half-integer
  spin sector the two lifts $\pm U_{s}(W)$ of one rotation $\rho(W)$ differ
  by the central sign.
- **Units.** $\hbar>0$ is a fixed positive parameter of the statement; $L_{i}$
  and $S_{i}=J_{i}\hbar$ carry the unit of action, and no numerical value is
  asserted.

items.title: The orbital Casimir identity: the restrictions of the orbital generators to the degree-l blocks are spin-l models
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]]: $S^2$ with its
polar measure $\sigma$, the Hilbert space $L^{2}(S^2,\sigma)$ with inner
product linear in the first argument
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]), the complete orthonormal
family $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]), the blocks
$V_{l}:=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$, the finite span $H$,
the self-adjoint operators $L_{1},L_{2},L_{3}$ with $L_{3}=L_{z}$ and
$L_{i}Y_{lm}\in V_{l}$ for all $l,m,i$, and the diagonal sphere Laplacian $A$
with $AY_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}$. Then for every $l\ge0$:

(a) each $L_{i}$ leaves $V_{l}$ invariant, and the restriction
$L_{i}|_{V_{l}}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of the finite-dimensional
inner product space $V_{l}$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), with
$L_{3}Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$ for $-l\le m\le l$;

(b) the triple $\bigl((1/\hbar)L_{1}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{2}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{3}|_{V_{l}}\bigr)$
is unitarily equivalent to the spin-$l$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]; in particular
$$\sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F\qquad(F\in V_{l});$$

(c) for every $F$ in the finite span $H$ one has
$\sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}AF$.

The statement is a mathematical statement about the operators on
$L^{2}(S^2,\sigma)$; no physical interpretation as angular momentum of a
particle is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice; the sphere $S^2$ with polar measure
$\sigma$; the family $(Y_{lm})$, the blocks $V_l$, the finite span $H$; the
operators $L_1,L_2,L_3$; the diagonal operator $A$; a degree $l\ge0$; indices
$m,i$; a vector $F\in H$.

[F1] **Orbital generators.** Each $L_{i}$ is self-adjoint on
$L^{2}(S^{2},\sigma)$; for $F\in V_{l}$ with polynomial representative $p_{F}$
one has $L_{i}F=\mathrm{res}_{l}(-i\hbar D_{i}p_{F})$ with
$D_{i}p=(x\times\nabla p)_{i}$, so $L_{i}V_{l}\subseteq V_{l}$ and
$L_{i}H\subseteq H$; on $H$ one has $L_{3}=L_{z}$ with
$L_{3}Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$, and
$L_{i}L_{j}-L_{j}L_{i}=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}L_{k}$ for all $i,j$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] clauses
(a),(b),(c)).

[F2] **Sphere Laplacian and the basis of a block.** $A$ is self-adjoint with
$AY_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}$, the finite span $H$ is a core of $A$, and the
$Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}$ are orthonormal in $L^{2}(S^{2},\sigma)$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]] clauses
(a),(b), [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]); hence
$\dim V_{l}=2l+1$ ([[def-dimension]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).

[F3] **Finite restrictions are self-adjoint.** If a self-adjoint operator $T$
on a Hilbert space leaves a finite-dimensional subspace $W$ invariant, then
$T|_{W}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of $W$: for $x,y\in W$ one has
$\langle T|_{W}x,y\rangle=\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle=\langle x,T|_{W}y\rangle$
because $Ty\in W$ and $T$ is symmetric on its domain
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-linear-subspace]]).

[F4] **Block decomposition of a finite angular momentum triple.** If a
nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner product space $V$ carries
self-adjoint endomorphisms $J_{1},J_{2},J_{3}$ with
$[J_{1},J_{2}]=iJ_{3}$ and its cyclic companions, then there are
$r\ge1$ and $j_{1},\dots,j_{r}\in\frac12\mathbb N$ with
$\sum_{\nu}(2j_{\nu}+1)=\dim V$ and an orthonormal basis
$(v_{\nu,k})$ of $V$ such that, with $J_{\pm}:=J_{1}\pm iJ_{2}$ and
$J^{2}:=J_{1}^{2}+J_{2}^{2}+J_{3}^{2}$,
$$J_{3}v_{\nu,k}=(j_{\nu}-k)v_{\nu,k},\quad J_{\pm}v_{\nu,k}=\sqrt{k(2j_{\nu}-k+1)}\,v_{\nu,k\mp1},\quad J^{2}v_{\nu,k}=j_{\nu}(j_{\nu}+1)v_{\nu,k};$$
moreover $\dim\ker(J_{3}-MI)$ equals the number of blocks with
$j_{\nu}\in M+\mathbb Z$ and $j_{\nu}\ge M$, and the number of blocks with
$j_{\nu}=M$ equals $\dim\ker(J_{3}-MI)-\dim\ker(J_{3}-(M+1)I)$, for
$M\in\frac12\mathbb N$; on each block the map $v_{\nu,k}\mapsto e_{j_{\nu}-k}$
is a unitary equivalence of $(J_{1},J_{2},J_{3})$ with the spin-$j_{\nu}$
matrices, and $J^{2}$ is self-adjoint and commutes with $J_{1},J_{2},J_{3}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-block-decomposition]] clauses
(a),(b),(d), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (b)).

[F5] **Countable sums of weights.** The spectrum of $L_{3}$ on the finite
space $V_{l}$ consists of the numbers $\hbar m$, $m=-l,\dots,l$, each with
multiplicity one, because $(Y_{lm})_{m}$ is an orthonormal basis of $V_{l}$
consisting of eigenvectors by [F1], [F2]
([[def-dimension]], [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; restrict the self-adjoint generators to the
finite blocks, invoke the finite-dimensional classification of angular
momentum triples, and identify the single block and its parameter from the
simple weight spectrum of $L_{3}$.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Invariance and finite self-adjointness] Fix $l$; by [F1] $L_{i}V_{l}\subseteq V_{l}$, and by [F3] applied to the invariant finite-dimensional subspace $V_{l}\subset L^{2}(S^{2},\sigma)$ the restriction $L_{i}|_{V_{l}}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of $V_{l}$; by [F1] and [F2], $L_{3}Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$ for every $m$ with $|m|\le l$, which is (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Angular momentum relations on the block] Put $J_{i}:=(1/\hbar)L_{i}|_{V_{l}}$; by step 1.1 the $J_{i}$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_{l}$ and by [F1] they satisfy $[J_{i},J_{j}]=i\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}J_{k}$ on $V_{l}$; moreover $J^{2}:=\sum_{i}J_{i}^{2}$ commutes with each $J_{i}$ by [F4] clause (a), and the eigenvalues of $J_{3}$ on $V_{l}$, read in units of $\hbar$, are $-l,-l+1,\dots,l$, each simple by [F5]. [step 1.1, F1, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Single block of parameter $l$] By step 2.1 and [F4] applied to the nonzero finite-dimensional space $V_{l}$ with the triple $(J_{1},J_{2},J_{3})$, there are $r\ge1$ and parameters $j_{\nu}\in\frac12\mathbb N$ whose weights $j_{\nu}-k$, $0\le k\le2j_{\nu}$, make up the spectrum of $J_{3}$; since every weight of an integer parameter is an integer and every weight of $J_{3}$ is an integer by step 2.1, no parameter is a non-integer half-integer, and [F4] applied with $M=0$ gives $r=\dim\ker J_{3}=1$ because $0$ is a simple eigenvalue of $J_{3}$; applying [F4] with $M=l$ gives $1=\dim\ker(J_{3}-lI)-\dim\ker(J_{3}-(l+1)I)$, so the unique parameter equals $l$; hence $J^{2}=l(l+1)\mathrm{id}_{V_{l}}$ by [F4], that is $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ for every $F\in V_{l}$, and the block basis of [F4] exhibits the unitary equivalence to the spin-$l$ matrices, which is (b). [step 2.1, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Finite span] Let $F\in H$; as a finite linear combination $F=\sum_{l,m}c_{lm}Y_{lm}$, the identities of step 3.1 apply to each term because $Y_{lm}\in V_{l}$, and $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\sum_{l,m}c_{lm}\hbar^{2}l(l+1)Y_{lm}=\hbar^{2}AF$ by the diagonal definition of $A$ in [F2] and the linearity of the finite sums. [step 3.1, F2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the block argument is not circular.** The classification theorem
  [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-block-decomposition]] is applied to
  the finite restrictions $(1/\hbar)L_{i}|_{V_{l}}$; the Casimir eigenvalue is
  then identified from the weight spectrum already present in
  [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]], and no
  differential identity for $\sum_{i}D_{i}^{2}$ is assumed.
- **Scope.** The identity concerns the operators on $L^{2}(S^{2},\sigma)$ and
  their finite harmonic span; no domain statement for a maximal operator
  $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}$ on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ is made here.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Section 2, printed pages 11-18: the algebraic angular momentum multiplets, J^2 eigenvalue j(j+1) and the ladder conditions

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Sections 8.1-8.2, printed pages 173-178 (PDF pages 185-190): position and momentum, angular momentum, the rotation group generated by the orbital generators and the simultaneous eigenbasis theorem

items.title: Orbital, spin and total angular momentum of the massive spin-s model: assigned sharp observables, units and readings
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor
assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6, all read for the
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$, and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ be its
componentwise Schwartz class
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]). Units are
those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the unit of angular
momentum is the unit of action (J$\,$s).

**(b) Orbital angular momentum.** For $i=1,2,3$ let $L_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]], the Stone
generator of the coordinate rotation group $t\mapsto U(R_{i}(t))$, so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ and, on the Schwartz class,
$$L_{i}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi$$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clause (b),
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The model reads
$(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an **assigned sharp observable**, called the
$i$-th **orbital angular momentum** of the model, with outcome law
$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). The operators
$L_{i}$ act on the spatial factor only; their reading on the angular degrees
of freedom is the one supplied by the sphere operators
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and the finite-blocks identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span is the content of a
separate lemma of this page
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]]).

**(c) Spin angular momentum.** Let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the internal
operators of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause
(c), the matrix actions $\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)_{l}=\hbar\sum_{m}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}$
of the self-adjoint matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]. The model reads
$(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the $i$-th **spin
angular momentum**; on the internal factor,
$$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k},\qquad S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)). The
**ladder** operators $S_{\pm}:=S_{x}\pm iS_{y}$ and the finite projections on
the basis vectors $e_{m}$ are structural objects of the internal factor, not
assigned sharp observables, and $S_{\pm}$ are not self-adjoint. For $s=\tfrac12$
one has $S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)). The internal
factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping factor: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Total angular momentum.** For each $i$ let
$$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}:=L_{i}+S_{i},\qquad D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}):=D(L_{i}),$$
the self-adjoint sum of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c)
(well defined because $S_{i}$ is bounded and strongly commutes with $L_{i}$;
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clause (a),
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). The model reads
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the
$i$-th **total angular momentum**; its flow is the coordinate subgroup
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ of the lifted rotation action,
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses (b),(c)).

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the angular momentum vocabulary
of this page within P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited readings. No new
physical assumption is added; in particular no magnetic coupling, no
spin-orbit interaction, no SU(2) gauge structure and no anomaly is
introduced. Whether a laboratory angular momentum measurement is described by
one of the assigned pairs $(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$, $(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ or
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ is a tested identification with
uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a
consequence of this definition; no measurement procedure, apparatus,
resolution or empirical value is supplied here. Antiunitary symmetries,
superselection rules and symmetries of preparations as opposed to dynamics
are outside the definition.

## Remarks

- **Why the sum is a definition and not a theorem.** The operator identity
  $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ requires the strong commutation of the
  two summands for self-adjointness of the sum; that commutation and the
  product-flow identity are proved in
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]], and this
  definition only names the resulting assigned observable.
- **Orbital and spin are distinct.** $L_{i}$ acts on the spatial factor and
  $S_{i}$ on the internal factor; no term of this definition identifies the
  spin with a rotation of a spatial body, and the page proves no spin-orbit
  coupling.
items.physical_scope: The angular momentum readings of the massive spin-s particle model: the orbital generators of the spatial coordinate rotations, the internal spin matrices of the spin assignment P6, and their self-adjoint sum, each read as an assigned sharp observable of the framework with units of action, together with the declaration that the internal factor is not a spatial object. The item fixes terminology and readings of P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6; it asserts no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus or detection model, no spin-orbit or relativistic structure and no empirical identification of any laboratory quantity with the operators named.

items.title: Effective magnetic-moment coupling of the finite-spin model: gyromagnetic parameter, magnetic moment and Zeeman energy operator
items.statement:
## Postulate

Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, for the declared massive
spin-$s$ particle model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and only within the
scope stated below, the following **effective magnetic-moment coupling**
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]).

**(i) Gyromagnetic parameter and magnetic moment.** For the declared spin
label $s$ assign a real **gyromagnetic parameter** $\gamma_{s}$, with unit
$\mathrm{s^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$, and define the **magnetic moment** of the model as
the internal-factor operator
$$\boldsymbol\mu:=\gamma_{s}\mathbf S=(\gamma_{s}S_{1},\gamma_{s}S_{2},\gamma_{s}S_{3}),$$
with unit $\mathrm{J\,T^{-1}}$. Here $\mathbf S=(S_{1},S_{2},S_{3})$ are the
spin operators of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] read on
the internal factor as in
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c). The
parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is an empirical model parameter of the species: it is
part of the declared model data, with uncertainty, and it is not derived from
$s$, from the mass parameter $m$ or from the charge of the particle; no
relation between $\gamma_{s}$ and any other species parameter is asserted by
this postulate.

**(ii) Prescribed field and Zeeman energy operator.** Let
$\mathbf B:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be a real bounded measurable
vector field, the **prescribed magnetic field profile**, with components
$B_{i}$ in tesla, entering the model as externally prescribed data
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]); in the
declared inertial frame the model adopts the **Zeeman energy operator**
$$H_{Z}:=H_{0}+M_{W},\qquad H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad M_{W}f:=-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\gamma_{s}B_{i}(\cdot)\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)(\cdot),$$
on the componentwise domain
$D(H_{Z}):=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, the domain of $H_{0}$
(componentwise, [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]];
$\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ is the componentwise free operator with that domain by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) applied to each component). The added term $M_{W}$ is bounded with
$\|M_{W}\|\le|\gamma_{s}|\sum_{i}\|B_{i}\|_{\infty}\max_{i}\|S_{i}\|$, so
$H_{Z}$ is a bounded self-adjoint perturbation of $H_{0}$ on the unchanged
domain, with unit joule, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$ is
a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group read in the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). The profile
$\mathbf B$ is a model input; the items of this page assert neither the
Maxwell equations nor a source or boundary realization of $\mathbf B$, and
the boundedness of $\mathbf B$ is an explicit hypothesis, not a general
property of magnetic fields.

**(iii) What is assumed and what is not.** (a) The coupling
$-\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B(Q)$ is an **effective interaction**: it is
adopted, not derived from the spin representation P6, from the
minimal-coupling postulate P5a of the framework or from classical
electromagnetism. (b) No value of $\gamma_{s}$ and no comparison with
measured gyromagnetic ratios or $g$-factors is made here. (c) No spin-orbit
coupling, no fine or hyperfine structure, no relativistic correction and no
radiation reaction is included. (d) A time-dependent field profile requires
its own domain and evolution hypotheses and is outside this postulate. (e)
The internal factor is not a spatial current distribution and $\boldsymbol\mu$
is not asserted to arise from a rotating charge distribution.

(iv) **Status.** This postulate is an adopted model assumption with the
physical scope above; it is motivated by and formulated after the cited
sources, which treat the coupling as a model input, and no deduction of it
from the framework's other postulates is claimed.

## Remarks

- **Why a bounded profile.** The domain statement is that of the free
  operator on $W^{2,2}$; it does not cover linearly growing fields, point
  dipoles or fields whose components leave $L^{\infty}$, each of which would
  require a separate form-domain or resolvent analysis.
- **Units check.** $\gamma_{s}$ in $\mathrm{s^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$ times $S_{i}$ in
  $\mathrm{J\,s}$ gives $\mathrm{J\,T^{-1}}$ for $\mu_{i}$, and
  $\mu_{i}B_{i}$ in $\mathrm{J\,T^{-1}\cdot T}=\mathrm{J}$; the phase
  $H_{Z}t/\hbar$ is dimensionless. The parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is read in the
  conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; no numerical
  value is asserted and, in particular, no exact value of any $g$-factor is
  assumed.

The item asserts no Maxwell equation, no source model, no derivation of gamma_s from charge and mass, no spin-orbit or relativistic correction, no dynamics and no measured value; it is a model assumption adopted on this page only.

items.title: Spin spectra and outcome laws of the massive spin-s model: directional components, the Casimir law and the spin-half probabilities
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]), and assume
the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ be the
outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in the pure preparation of a
unit vector $\psi$, and for a unit vector $n=(n_{1},n_{2},n_{3})\in\mathbb
R^{3}$ put $S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$, the matrix action of the self-adjoint
matrix $\hbar\,n\cdot J$ on the internal factor. Then:

(a) for every unit $n$ the operator $S_{n}$ is a bounded self-adjoint
operator on $H_{s}$ with spectrum
$\sigma(S_{n})=\hbar\{-s,-s+1,\dots,s\}$, and for each
$m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}$ the eigenspace $\ker(S_{n}-\hbar m)$ is the range of the
fibrewise orthogonal projection $P_{n,m}$ onto the eigenline of the matrix
$n\cdot J$ with eigenvalue $m$; consequently, for every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$,
$$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar m\})=\|P_{n,m}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{n,m}\psi,\psi\rangle\qquad(m=-s,\dots,s),$$
and the law is concentrated on the finite set $\hbar\{-s,\dots,s\}$;

(b) the Casimir operator $S^{2}=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}$ equals
$\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$ as a bounded operator, so for every preparation $\rho$ the
law of $S^{2}$ is the Dirac law at $\hbar^{2}s(s+1)$, and one has the
commutation relations
$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k}$ and
$[S^{2},S_{i}]=0$ on $H_{s}$, componentwise on the internal factor;

(c) for $s=\tfrac12$, every unit $n$ and every unit $\psi\in H_{1/2}$ one has
$$P_{n,\pm}=\tfrac12\bigl(I\pm n\cdot\sigma\bigr),\qquad \mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr) =\frac{1}{2}\Bigl(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle\Bigr),$$
where $n\cdot\sigma$ is applied fibrewise; in particular,
$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})+\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=1$ and
each number lies in $[0,1]$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5 and
P6 and the cited finite-dimensional mathematics; they concern the internal
factor of the model. They assert no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no
measurement or apparatus model, no joint measurement of two spin components,
no value of $\hbar$ and no empirical spin value. In particular the statements
do not identify the operators $S_{n}$ with any laboratory spin measurement,
and they contain no comparison with data.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the stated readings; the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; the spin-s model with parameters
$m>0$, $s$ and $r=2s+1$; the internal matrices $J_{i}$ and the spin
operators $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$; a unit vector $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$; the
operator $S_{n}$; a unit vector $\psi\in H_{s}$; a preparation $\rho$;
indices $i,j,k$ and eigenvalues $\lambda$ of a self-adjoint operator.

[F1] **Finite spin matrices.** On $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{r}$ the matrices $J_{i}$
are self-adjoint with $[J_{i},J_{j}]=i\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}J_{k}$,
$J^{2}=J_{x}^{2}+J_{y}^{2}+J_{z}^{2}=s(s+1)I$, $J_{\pm}=J_{x}\pm iJ_{y}$,
$[J^{2},J_{i}]=0$, and the basis $(e_{m})$ satisfies
$J_{z}e_{m}=me_{m}$, $J_{\pm}e_{m}=\sqrt{(s\mp m)(s\pm m+1)}e_{m\pm1}$; for
$s=\tfrac12$ one has $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ with
$\sigma_{i}\sigma_{j}+\sigma_{j}\sigma_{i}=2\delta_{ij}I$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),(d),(e)).

[F2] **Finite angular momentum classification.** If a nonzero
finite-dimensional complex inner product space $V$ carries self-adjoint
endomorphisms $A_{1},A_{2},A_{3}$ with $[A_{1},A_{2}]=iA_{3}$ and its cyclic
companions, then $V$ is an orthogonal direct sum of blocks on each of which
the triple is unitarily equivalent to a spin-$j$ model with
$A^{2}=j(j+1)I$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-block-decomposition]] clauses
(b),(c), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]).

[F3] **Model operators as matrix actions.** The model's $S_{n}$ is the
fibrewise matrix action $(S_{n}f)(x)=\hbar(n\cdot J)f(x)$ on
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ of a self-adjoint matrix, hence
bounded self-adjoint with $\|S_{n}\|\le\hbar\|n\cdot J\|$
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c),
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
clause (c), [[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]).

[F4] **Eigenvalues and their spectral weights.** If $\lambda$ is an
eigenvalue of a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral projection-valued
measure $E_{A}$, then $E_{A}(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto
$\ker(A-\lambda)$; for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ one has
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=\|E_{A}(\{\lambda\})\psi\|^{2}$
([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses
(a),(b), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (b)).

[F5] **Reading of the readings.** The model's angular momentum operators are
the assigned sharp observables of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clauses
(b),(c) with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$; the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable is that of P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), and
the pure preparations are those of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; for an arbitrary direction realize the rotated
triple and apply the finite angular momentum classification to obtain a single
spin-$s$ block, then read the eigenspaces as ranges of fibrewise projections
and compute the law with the atom formula; the spin-half case is evaluated in
the Pauli matrices.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Directional component is a single spin-$s$ block] Fix a unit $n$ and choose an oriented orthonormal frame $(e^{(1)},e^{(2)},e^{(3)})$ of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with $e^{(1)}=n$; put $A_{i}:=\sum_{l}e^{(i)}_{l}J_{l}$ for $i=1,2,3$; expanding the commutator with [F1] gives $[A_{i},A_{j}]=\sum_{l,m}e^{(i)}_{l}e^{(j)}_{m}[J_{l},J_{m}]=i\sum_{k}\bigl(\sum_{l,m}\varepsilon_{lmk}e^{(i)}_{l}e^{(j)}_{m}\bigr)J_{k}=i\sum_{k}(e^{(i)}\times e^{(j)})_{k}J_{k}$, which equals $iA_{i'}$ with $i'$ the index for which $e^{(i)}\times e^{(j)}=e^{(i')}$, and $\sum_{i}A_{i}^{2}=\sum_{k}J_{k}^{2}=s(s+1)I$ by the orthonormality of the frame; by [F2] applied to the triple $(A_{1},A_{2},A_{3})$ there is a decomposition into blocks with parameters $j_{\nu}$ satisfying $j_{\nu}(j_{\nu}+1)=s(s+1)$ on each block, so $j_{\nu}=s$ and every block has dimension $2s+1=\dim V_{s}$; hence there is exactly one block and $A_{1}=n\cdot J$ has the simple eigenvalues $s,s-1,\dots,-s$, which is the spectrum statement of (a) at the matrix level. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Fibrewise spectral measure and law of $S_{n}$] By step 1.1 the matrix $n\cdot J$ has the simple eigenvalues $m=-s,\dots,s$; let $P_{n,m}$ be the fibrewise action on $H_{s}$ of the orthogonal projection of $\mathbb C^{r}$ onto the eigenline of $n\cdot J$ with eigenvalue $m$; each $P_{n,m}$ is an orthogonal projection on $H_{s}$, $P_{n,m}P_{n,m'}=0$ for $m\ne m'$, $\sum_{m}P_{n,m}=I$ fibrewise, and $S_{n}=\sum_{m}\hbar mP_{n,m}$ as bounded operators; consequently $\ker(S_{n}-\hbar m)=\operatorname{ran}P_{n,m}$ because a class $f$ satisfies $\hbar(n\cdot J)f(x)=\hbar mf(x)$ for almost every $x$ exactly when $f(x)$ lies in the $m$-eigenline almost everywhere; by [F4] applied to the self-adjoint $S_{n}$ of [F3], $E_{S_{n}}(\{\hbar m\})=P_{n,m}$ and $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar m\})=\|P_{n,m}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{n,m}\psi,\psi\rangle$ for every unit $\psi$; since $\sum_{m}P_{n,m}=I$, the law is concentrated on $\hbar\{-s,\dots,s\}$, which is (a). [step 1.1, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Coordinate components, Casimir and commutators] Applying step 2.1 with $n$ a standard basis vector gives clause (a) for the coordinate components $S_{i}$; by [F1] the matrices satisfy $[J_{i},J_{j}]=i\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}J_{k}$ and $J^{2}=s(s+1)I$, which pass to the fibrewise actions: $[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k}$ and $S^{2}=\hbar^{2}J^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$ as bounded operators, so $[S^{2},S_{i}]=0$; since $S^{2}$ is a scalar operator, its law in every preparation is the Dirac law at $\hbar^{2}s(s+1)$, which is (b). [step 2.1, F1, F3, algebra]

3.2 [Spin-half probabilities] Let $s=\tfrac12$ and let $n$ be unit; by [F1], $(n\cdot\sigma)^{2}=\sum_{i,j}n_{i}n_{j}\sigma_{i}\sigma_{j}=\sum_{i,j}n_{i}n_{j}\delta_{ij}I=I$, so $n\cdot\sigma$ is a self-adjoint involution with eigenvalues $\pm1$, and $P_{\pm}:=\tfrac12(I\pm n\cdot\sigma)$ are orthogonal projections with $P_{+}+P_{-}=I$ and $(n\cdot\sigma)P_{\pm}=\pm P_{\pm}$; hence $P_{\pm}$ are the eigenline projections of $n\cdot J=\tfrac12n\cdot\sigma$ for the eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac12$, and step 2.1 gives $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\})=\|P_{\pm}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{\pm}\psi,\psi\rangle=\tfrac12(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle)$, which lies in $[0,1]$ because $P_{\pm}$ are projections and sums to $1$; this is (c). [step 2.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 2.1 proves (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 3.2 proves (c); clauses (a)-(c) used only the internal matrices, the readings of [F5] and the atom formula [F4], no dynamics, coupling, apparatus or empirical input entered, which is the scope statement (d). [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, F5] ∎

## Remarks

- **Simplicity of the directional eigenvalues.** The simplicity of the
  eigenvalues of $n\cdot J$ is a statement about the internal matrices; the
  corresponding eigenspaces of $S_{n}$ on $H_{s}$ are infinite-dimensional
  (spatial functions times one internal vector), and clause (a) records the
  Born weight of the fibrewise projection, not a finite-dimensional
  multiplicity.
- **No joint law.** Nothing in this theorem asserts a joint outcome law of two
  different components $S_{n}$ and $S_{n'}$ with $n$ not parallel to $n'$; the
  incompatibility of the components is a separate result of the uncertainty
  page, and the present item uses no joint measurement model.

The item concerns the internal factor only; it asserts no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus model, no measured spin value and no empirical identification of the operators.
