items.title: Orbital angular momentum eigenstates of the massive model: spherical harmonics, the l,m quantum numbers and the Casimir value
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and
the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $l\ge0$, $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$, a unit vector
$w\in\mathbb C^{r}$ and a complex-valued $R\in C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty))$, and
let $h_{lm}$ be the harmonic homogeneous polynomial of degree $l$ with
$h_{lm}|_{S^2}=Y_{lm}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]] clause (c)
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]). Define
the model vector
$$\psi(x):=R(|x|)\,h_{lm}(x)\,w\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3},\ x\ne0),\qquad \psi(0):=0 .$$
Then:

(a) $\psi$ is a well-defined class in the model's state space $H_{s}$ and in
fact $\psi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})\subseteq\mathcal
S^{(r)}$; it lies in $D(L_{i})$ for each $i$, and for $x\ne0$
$$(L_{i}\psi)(x)=R(|x|)\,\bigl(-i\hbar\,D_{i}h_{lm}\bigr)(x)\,w,\qquad D_{i}h_{lm}=(x\times\nabla h_{lm})_{i},$$
so that $-i\hbar D_{i}h_{lm}$ is the polynomial representative of the sphere
function $L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]]; in particular
$L_{3}\psi=\hbar m\,\psi$;

(b) with $\|R\|_{l}^{2}:=\int_{0}^{\infty}|R(r)|^{2}r^{2l+2}\,dr$ one has
$\|\psi\|^{2}=\|R\|_{l}^{2}$ and
$$\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}=\|R\|_{l}^{2}\,\bigl\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\bigr\|^{2}, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{3}\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)\,\|\psi\|^{2},$$
so the Casimir quadratic form of the model's orbital generators on $\psi$
takes the value $\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$;

(c) consequently, for the pure preparation of the unit vector
$\psi/\|\psi\|$ (for $R\not\equiv0$), the mean and the second moment of the
outcome law of $(L_{3},\mathrm{J\,s})$ are finite and equal
$\hbar m$ and $\hbar^{2}m^{2}$, so the variance vanishes; for each $i$ the
mean and second moment of the law of $L_{i}$ are finite and the second moment
equals $\bigl\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\bigr\|^{2}$; the model reads $(l,m)$
as the **orbital angular momentum quantum numbers** of the preparation, in
the sense of the eigenvalue of the angular momentum-squared form and the
eigenvalue of $L_{3}$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, P6
and the cited mathematics, and concern the spatial factor of the massive
model. The item asserts no dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no
joint sharp values of two different components $L_{i},L_{j}$, no empirical
value and no spectral resolution of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$: the identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$ is a quadratic-form statement on the
displayed smooth vectors and is not read as a statement about a self-adjoint
operator $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}$ on the full spatial Hilbert space.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the stated readings; the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; the model with parameters $m>0$,
$s$, $r=2s+1$; the harmonic polynomial $h_{lm}$ and the sphere functions
$Y_{lm}$; the radial function $R$; the unit vector $w$; the vector $\psi$;
indices $i,k$.

[F1] **Harmonic polynomial and spherical harmonic.** For $l\ge0$ and
$-l\le m\le l$ the polynomial $h_{lm}$ is homogeneous of degree $l$, harmonic,
nonzero, with $h_{lm}|_{S^2}=Y_{lm}$, and $D_{3}h_{lm}=im\,h_{lm}$ where
$D_{3}=x_{1}\partial_{2}-x_{2}\partial_{1}$; moreover $L_{3}^{\mathrm{sph}}
Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$ and $L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}
=\mathrm{res}_{l}(-i\hbar D_{i}h_{lm})$ for $D_{i}p=(x\times\nabla p)_{i}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]] clause (c),
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] clauses
(a),(c), [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]
clause (c)).

[F2] **Core action of the orbital generators.** For every componentwise
Schwartz class $\varphi\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$ the orbital generators satisfy
$L_{i}\varphi\in H_{s}$, $\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq D(L_{i})$, and
$$L_{i}\varphi=-i\hbar\sum_{j}(e_{i}\times x)_{j}D_{j}\varphi=\sum_{j,k}\varepsilon_{ijk}Q_{j}P_{k}\varphi ,$$
with $D_{j}$ the componentwise weak derivative
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clauses
(a),(b), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clauses (a),(c)).

[F3] **Orbital Casimir identity.** For $F\in V_{l}$ one has
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span, and the
on-shell values are exactly the squared norms
$\sum_{i}\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]] clauses (b),(c),
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]]).

[F4] **Polar integration and the sphere measure.** For a Borel
$f\ge0$ on $\mathbb R^{3}$ one has
$\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}f\,dx=\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{S^{2}}f(r\Omega)\,r^{2}d\sigma(\Omega)\,dr$,
and $\int_{S^{2}}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\circ\Phi\,\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$
with $\sigma(S^{2})=4\pi$
([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]],
[[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]]).

[F5] **Schwartz calculus and the class reading.** $C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb
R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$; a classical partial
derivative of a $C^{1}$ function that is locally integrable is its weak
derivative; the model space consists of almost-everywhere classes
([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]],
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; the vector is a compactly supported smooth class
with a homogeneous polynomial angular factor, so the core identity of the
generators applies; the radial and angular integrals separate by polar
integration and the Casimir value is transported from the sphere.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Smoothness and the polynomial identity] Since $\operatorname{supp}R\subseteq[a,b]$ with $0<a\le b<\infty$ and $h_{lm}$ is a polynomial, the function $\psi=R(|x|)h_{lm}(x)w$ vanishes identically near $0$ and is smooth on $\mathbb R^{3}$ with compact support, so $\psi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$ by [F5]; for $x\ne0$ and each $i$, the product rule gives $(x\times\nabla)_{i}\psi=R(|x|)(D_{i}h_{lm})(x)w$ because $(x\times\nabla)_{i}R(|x|)=R'(|x|)\,(x\times x)_{i}/|x|=0$, and by [F1] the function $-i\hbar D_{i}h_{lm}$ is the polynomial representative of $L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}$; moreover [F1] gives $D_{3}h_{lm}=im\,h_{lm}$. [F1, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Core action and $L_{3}$ eigenvalue] By step 1.1 and [F2], $\psi\in D(L_{i})$ and $L_{i}\psi=\sum_{j,k}\varepsilon_{ijk}Q_{j}P_{k}\psi=-i\hbar\,(x\times\nabla)_{i}\psi=R(|x|)\,(-i\hbar D_{i}h_{lm})(x)\,w$ for almost every $x$, where the weak derivatives agree with the classical ones by [F5]; here $P_{k}=-i\hbar\partial_{k}$ on the Schwartz class, so the factor $-i\hbar$ occurs once. For $i=3$, [F1] gives $L_{3}\psi=-i\hbar R\,D_{3}h_{lm}\,w=\hbar mR\,h_{lm}w=\hbar m\psi$, proving (a). [step 1.1, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Norms and the Casimir form] Put $q_i:=D_i h_{lm}$. Each term $x_j\partial_k h_{lm}$ is homogeneous of degree $l$ or zero, so $q_i(r\Omega)=r^lq_i(\Omega)$ for $r>0$; for $l=0$, $q_i=0$. By step 2.1, $\|w\|=1$ and polar integration [F4], $\|L_i\psi\|^2=\hbar^2\int_{\mathbb R^3}|R(|x|)|^2|q_i(x)|^2\,dx=\hbar^2\bigl(\int_0^\infty|R(r)|^2r^{2l+2}\,dr\bigr)\int_{S^2}|q_i(\Omega)|^2\,d\sigma(\Omega)$. By [F1], $L_i^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}=-i\hbar q_i|_{S^2}$, hence $\|L_i\psi\|^2=\|R\|_l^2\|L_i^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\|^2$. Likewise homogeneity of $h_{lm}$ and [F4] give $\|\psi\|^2=\|R\|_l^2\int_{S^2}|Y_{lm}|^2\,d\sigma=\|R\|_l^2$, using the normalization in [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] clause (d). Finally, on the finite invariant block $V_l$, self-adjointness and [F3] give $\sum_i\|L_i^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\|^2=\langle\sum_i(L_i^{\mathrm{sph}})^2Y_{lm},Y_{lm}\rangle=\hbar^2l(l+1)$, so $\sum_i\|L_i\psi\|^2=\hbar^2l(l+1)\|\psi\|^2$, proving (b), including $l=0$ and $R=0$. [step 2.1, F1, F3, F4, given, algebra]

4.1 [Readings] Let $R\not\equiv0$ and put $\varphi:=\psi/\|\psi\|$; by step 2.1, $L_{3}\varphi=\hbar m\varphi$ with $\varphi\in D(L_{3})$, so the mean and the second moment of the law of $L_{3}$ in the pure preparation $[\varphi]$ are $\langle L_{3}\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\hbar m$ and $\|L_{3}\varphi\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}m^{2}$, with variance $0$; for each $i$, step 2.1 gives $\varphi\in D(L_{i})$ and step 3.1 gives $\|L_{i}\varphi\|^{2}=\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\|^{2}$, so the mean and second moment of the law of $L_{i}$ are finite with that second moment, and the quadratic form is $\sum_{i}\|L_{i}\varphi\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$, which is (c). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3, algebra]

5.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 4.1 proves (c); only the spatial core identities, the sphere data and polar integration were used, no dynamics, apparatus or empirical input entered, and no operator identity for $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}$ on the full space was asserted, which is the scope statement (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F2] ∎

## Remarks

- **The density of the family.** The vectors $R(|x|)h_{lm}(x)w$ with
  $R\in C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty))$ span a dense subspace of the angular
  sector $L^{2}((0,\infty),r^{2}dr)\otimes\mathbb C\,Y_{lm}\otimes\mathbb C w$
  in the polar decomposition; this theorem uses only their eigenproperty and
  makes no completeness claim.
- **No hidden operator $(L^{2})$.** The Casimir value is stated as a
  quadratic-form identity. Defining a self-adjoint operator $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}$
  on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ would require a separate closed-form and domain
  argument, which is not part of this page.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of P1, P2, P5 and P6 for the massive spin-s model and its orbital generators: for a smooth compactly supported radial profile times a spherical harmonic, the model vector is an eigenvector of the third orbital generator with eigenvalue hbar m, the Casimir quadratic form takes the value hbar^2 l(l+1), and the orbital quantum numbers are those of the spherical harmonic family. The statement concerns the spatial factor only, uses no dynamics and no measurement model, and asserts no spectral decomposition of the full spatial Hilbert space, no hydrogen spectrum and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 7.2, printed pages 145-154 (PDF pages 153-162): spherical harmonics as angular momentum eigenfunctions with quantum numbers l and m and the eigenvalue l(l+1) of the Casimir

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 4.1-4.1.2, printed pages 96-103 (PDF pages 99-106): orbital angular momentum, the commutators, the l,m quantum numbers and the l = 0 exceptions

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Section 1, printed pages 1-11: orbital angular momentum and the spherical harmonic eigenvalues in the radial problem

items.title: Conservation of total angular momentum for a spin-independent rotation-invariant bounded-potential dynamics
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) and the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Let $V:\mathbb
R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable with
$V\circ R^{-1}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$, let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
be the model's spin-independent bounded-potential energy operator on
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with flow
$U(t)=e^{-itH_{V}/\hbar}$ in the reading of P4, and let
$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ be the total angular momenta of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(d). Then:

(a) for each $i$ the lifted coordinate rotation family
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c) is a
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of symmetries of the declared
dynamics: $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))\,U(u)=U(u)\,U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ for all $t,u$ and
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$;

(b) each $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable of
the model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
and for a unit vector $\psi\in D(L_{i})=D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}})$ the mean and
the second moment of the law of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ in the pure
preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero
values $\langle J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and
$\|J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi\|^{2}$;

(c) in the same situation each spin component $S_{i}$ and each orbital
generator $L_{i}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable in the same sense,
the laws of $S_{i}$ and $L_{i}$ being time-independent in every preparation;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
cited results, and concerns the declared isolated model with a real bounded
measurable potential invariant under every spatial rotation. It asserts no
symmetry of any concrete external field or apparatus, excludes spin-dependent,
singular and unbounded potentials (which require their own domain and symmetry
arguments), introduces no measurement, detector or empirical record, and
makes no claim that a definite numerical value of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is
revealed at each time: the conserved object is the outcome law.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the stated readings; the
three choice principles; the model parameters $m>0$, $s$, $r=2s+1$; the
rotationally invariant real bounded measurable potential $V$; the energy
operator $H_{V}$ and its flow $U$; the angular momentum operators $L_{i}$,
$S_{i}$, $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$; a preparation $\rho$; a Borel set $B$;
times $t,u$; a unit vector $\psi$.

[F1] **The bounded-potential operator.** $H_{V}$ is self-adjoint on
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ as the componentwise sum of
the free operator and the bounded multiplier $M_{V}$, its domain is invariant
under the flow $U(t)=e^{-itH_{V}/\hbar}$, which is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group, and $P_{k},M_{V}$ act componentwise
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (b),(c) applied to each component,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Rotation invariance of the model.** For every $R\in SO(3)$ one has
$U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$ with $V_{R}(x)=V(R^{-1}x)$; since $V_{R}=V$
almost everywhere by hypothesis, every $U(R)$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
clause (b), the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry
group, and each $L_{i}$ is conserved with time-independent law and moments in
the sense of that page
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F3] **Lifted coordinate group.** For every $i$,
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=U(R_{i}(t))M_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with
$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ self-adjoint on $D(L_{i})$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses
(b),(c)).

[F4] **Componentwise commutation with internal matrices.** The fibrewise
matrix action $M$ of any fixed matrix commutes with the componentwise
operators $P_{k}$ and $M_{V}$ and preserves their common domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$; hence it commutes with $H_{V}$ on
$D(H_{V})$. If a bounded self-adjoint $S$ satisfies $SK\subseteq KS$ for a
self-adjoint $K$, then $Se^{-itK/\hbar}=e^{-itK/\hbar}S$ for every $t$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (d),
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conserved-spectral-probability-laws]]
clause (a')).

[F5] **Conservation from a symmetry group.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned
sharp observable with $W(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}$ for a self-adjoint $A$. If
$W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t$, then the outcome law of $(A,u_{A})$ is
time-independent in every preparation, and if $\psi\in D(A)$ is a unit vector
the mean and second moment of the law in $[\psi(t)]$ are finite and
independent of $t$ with time-zero values $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and
$\|A\psi\|^{2}$
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] clauses (a),(b),
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
[[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; combine the rotational invariance of the bounded
potential with the componentwise commutation of the internal matrices, verify
the symmetry property of the lifted coordinate groups, and read the
conservation statement from the generator-conservation theorem.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Internal factors commute with the dynamics] Let $M$ be the fibrewise matrix action of a fixed matrix; by [F4] $M$ commutes with $P_{k}$ and with $M_{V}$ and preserves $W^{2,2}$, hence $MD(H_{V})\subseteq D(H_{V})$, $M(H_{V}\psi)=H_{V}(M\psi)$ for $\psi\in D(H_{V})$, and $MU(t)=U(t)M$ for every $t$ by the second part of [F4]; in particular this applies to $M=M_{s}(A_{i}(t))$, to $M=S_{i}$ and to every bounded matrix action. [F1, F4, algebra]

1.2 [Spatial rotations are symmetries] By the hypothesis $V\circ R^{-1}=V$ almost everywhere and [F2], every $U(R)$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, so $U(R)U(t)=U(t)U(R)$ for all $R,t$ and $U(R)D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$; in particular this holds for the coordinate rotations $U(R_{i}(t))$. [F2, algebra]

2.1 [Lifted coordinate groups are symmetries] Fix $i$ and $t$; by [F3], $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=U(R_{i}(t))M_{s}(A_{i}(t))$; by step 1.2 the first factor commutes with $U(u)$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$, and by step 1.1 the second factor does the same, so the product commutes with $U(u)$ for every $u$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$; combined with the group property and strong continuity of [F3], the family $t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of symmetries, which is (a). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F3, algebra]

2.2 [Spin and orbital components] By step 1.1 applied to $M=S_{i}$, the bounded self-adjoint $S_{i}$ satisfies $S_{i}H_{V}\subseteq H_{V}S_{i}$, so [F4] gives $S_{i}U(t)=U(t)S_{i}$ for every $t$; applying [F5] with $A:=S_{i}$ (bounded, so $W(s)=e^{-isS_{i}/\hbar}$ commutes with $U$) gives the time-independence of the law of $S_{i}$ in every preparation, and by [F2] the law and moments of each $L_{i}$ are time-independent as well, which is (c). [step 1.1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Total angular momentum conservation] By step 2.1 and [F3], the group $W(s):=e^{-isJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}=U_{s}(A_{i}(s))$ satisfies $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$; applying [F5] to the assigned sharp observable $(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ of [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause (d) gives the time-independence of its outcome law in every preparation and, for a unit $\psi\in D(L_{i})=D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}})$, the conservation of the mean and second moment with the stated time-zero values, which is (b). [step 2.1, F3, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 2.1 proves (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c); only the bounded-potential domain, the almost-everywhere rotational invariance and the lifted coordinate groups were used, no spin-dependent or singular potential, apparatus or empirical input entered, and the conserved object is the outcome law, which is the scope statement (d). [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, F1, F5] ∎

## Remarks

- **Where the spin-independence enters.** Step 1.1 uses only that the
  dynamics is componentwise in the internal factor. A spin-dependent
  potential (for instance a term $S_{z}B(Q_{x})$ as on the Zeeman page) does
  not commute with arbitrary internal matrices, and the conservation of
  $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ for such a dynamics requires its own analysis; the
  Zeeman page proves the weaker conservation of $S_{z}$ for a field along the
  third axis.
- **Orbital conservation is inherited.** Clause (c) records the orbital
  statement of the symmetries page in the vocabulary of this page; the new
  content of the theorem is the lifted group of (a) and the total angular
  momentum of (b).
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 for the declared isolated massive spin-s model with a real bounded measurable spin-independent potential invariant under every spatial rotation: the lifted coordinate rotation subgroups are one-parameter symmetry groups, and each total angular momentum component is a conserved assigned sharp observable whose outcome law is time-independent in every preparation, with conserved mean and second moment on D(L_i). The item asserts no symmetry of any concrete system, no spin-dependent or singular potential, no measurement procedure and no empirical result.

Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 4.3, printed pages 68-70 (PDF pages 76-78): symmetries imply conservation, including the conservation of angular momentum for rotation-invariant Hamiltonians; Section 7.4, printed pages 161-164 (spin in a rotation-invariant model)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Theorem 8.1 printed page 174 (PDF page 186) and Section 8.2 printed pages 175-178 (PDF pages 187-190): conserved quantities for rotation-invariant Schrodinger operators and the invariance of the domain of a conserved observable

items.title: Spin precession and the Zeeman splitting in a uniform magnetic field: Larmor angular frequency and the conservation of one component
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the effective magnetic-moment coupling
adopted in [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] and the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a real constant
$B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and use the uniform static field profile
$\mathbf B(x):=(0,0,B_{z})$, so that the Zeeman energy operator of the
postulate is
$$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3},\qquad H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
with flow $U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$, and put $\omega:=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$
with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. For a unit vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ put
$\psi(t):=U_{Z}(t)\psi$ and $\langle S_{i}\rangle(t):=\langle
S_{i}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$. Then:

(a) $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{Z})$ and
$$U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,e^{it\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
so in particular the transverse means satisfy, for every $t$,
$$\langle S_{1}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0)+\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0),\qquad \langle S_{2}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)-\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),$$
and the transverse vector $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(t),\langle S_{2}\rangle(t)\bigr)$
is the rotation of $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)\bigr)$
by the angle $-\omega t$ in the $(1,2)$-plane;

(b) the component along the field is conserved: $S_{3}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S_{3}$
and $\langle S_{3}\rangle(t)=\langle S_{3}\rangle(0)$ for every unit $\psi$
and every $t$; more generally the outcome law of $S_{3}$ is time-independent
in every preparation;

(c) the conjugation identities
$$e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{1}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{1}+\sin(\omega t)S_{2},\qquad e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{2}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{2}-\sin(\omega t)S_{1}$$
hold as bounded operator identities, and with $S^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$
(the Casimir operator of the model) also $S^{2}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S^{2}$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
adopted coupling; it concerns the uniform static field $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z})$
with $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and the declared isolated model. It excludes
inhomogeneous and time-dependent fields, spin-dependent spatial potentials,
radiation, relaxation and environment coupling, asserts no measured
precession frequency and no measured gyromagnetic parameter, and identifies
no apparatus: $\omega=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$ is a model quantity computed from
assigned model parameters.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the magnetic-moment
postulate in the stated readings; the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of
Countable Choice; the model parameters $m>0$, $s$, $r=2s+1$ and
$\gamma_{s}\in\mathbb R$; the field constant $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$; the
operators $H_{0}$, $H_{Z}$, $S_{i}$, $S^{2}$; a unit vector $\psi$; real
$t,\theta$.

[F1] **Free operator and componentwise structure.** $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint
on $D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with flow
$e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$; its terms $P_{k}$ act componentwise and commute with
every fibrewise matrix action, which preserves $W^{2,2}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) applied componentwise,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a),
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Magnetic-moment postulate.** With $\gamma_{s}\in\mathbb R$ and a real
bounded measurable profile $\mathbf B$, the Zeeman operator
$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{s}\sum_{i}S_{i}B_{i}(Q)$ with domain $D(H_{0})$ is a
bounded self-adjoint perturbation of $H_{0}$, of unit joule, and
$t\mapsto e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$ is its strongly continuous unitary group in the
reading of P4
([[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] clauses (i),(ii),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

[F3] **Product flow.** If a bounded self-adjoint $B$ commutes with the flow
$e^{iuA}$ of a self-adjoint $A$, then $A+B$ with domain $D(A)$ is
self-adjoint and $e^{-it(A+B)/\hbar}=e^{-itA/\hbar}e^{-itB/\hbar}$ for all
$t$ ([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clauses (a),(c)).

[F4] **Spin algebra and the ladder conjugation.** On the internal factor,
$[S_{3},S_{\pm}]=\pm\hbar S_{\pm}$ for $S_{\pm}=S_{1}\pm iS_{2}$,
$S_{1}=\tfrac12(S_{+}+S_{-})$, $S_{2}=\tfrac1{2i}(S_{+}-S_{-})$ and
$S^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$; for the bounded exponential,
$e^{i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}S_{\pm}e^{-i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}=e^{\pm i\theta}S_{\pm}$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),
[[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]],
[[def-operator-norm]]).

[F5] **Conserved law from commutation.** If a bounded self-adjoint $S$
satisfies $SK\subseteq KS$ for a self-adjoint $K$, then
$Se^{-itK/\hbar}=e^{-itK/\hbar}S$ for all $t$
([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conserved-spectral-probability-laws]]
clause (a')); and if an assigned sharp observable $A$ satisfies
$e^{-isA/\hbar}U(t)=U(t)e^{-isA/\hbar}$ for all $s,t$, then its outcome law is
time-independent in every preparation, with conserved mean and second moment
on $D(A)$
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] clauses (a),(b),
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
[[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; write the Zeeman operator as a bounded
perturbation commuting with the free flow, factor its evolution, conjugate the
spin components by the resulting internal rotation, and read conservation of
the field component from the commutation criterion.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Self-adjointness and factorization] The perturbation $B_{0}:=-\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}$ is bounded self-adjoint by [F4]; by [F1] it commutes with every element of the free flow $e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$ because it is a fibrewise matrix action commuting with the componentwise free operator; hence [F3] applies with $A:=H_{0}$ and $B:=B_{0}$, so $H_{Z}=H_{0}+B_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ and $e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}e^{it\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}$ for every $t$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

1.2 [Conjugation of the transverse components] By [F4] the map $\theta\mapsto g(\theta):=e^{i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}S_{+}e^{-i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}$ satisfies $g'(\theta)=e^{i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}(i/\hbar)[S_{3},S_{+}]e^{-i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}=ig(\theta)$ by the derivative formula of the bounded exponential, so $g(\theta)=e^{i\theta}S_{+}$; conjugating $S_{-}$ gives $e^{-i\theta}S_{-}$; taking real and imaginary parts via [F4] yields $e^{i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}S_{1}e^{-i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}=\cos\theta\,S_{1}-\sin\theta\,S_{2}$ and $e^{i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}S_{2}e^{-i\theta S_{3}/\hbar}=\sin\theta\,S_{1}+\cos\theta\,S_{2}$. [F4, algebra]

2.1 [Transverse means] By step 1.1, $U_{Z}(t)^{*}=e^{-it\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}e^{itH_{0}/\hbar}$, so using the commutation of $S_{1},S_{2}$ with $H_{0}$ from [F1], $U_{Z}(t)^{*}S_{1}U_{Z}(t)=e^{-i\omega tS_{3}/\hbar}S_{1}e^{i\omega tS_{3}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{1}+\sin(\omega t)S_{2}$ and $U_{Z}(t)^{*}S_{2}U_{Z}(t)=\cos(\omega t)S_{2}-\sin(\omega t)S_{1}$ by step 1.2 with $\theta=-\omega t$; taking expectations in the unit vector $\psi$ gives the two displayed mean identities, and the pair transformation is the rotation by $-\omega t$; this is (a) and the conjugation identities of (c). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, algebra]

2.2 [Conservation of the field component] By [F4] the bounded self-adjoint $S_{3}$ commutes with $H_{0}$ and with itself, hence $S_{3}H_{Z}\subseteq H_{Z}S_{3}$ on $D(H_{Z})$; [F5] gives $S_{3}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S_{3}$ for every $t$, so $\langle S_{3}\rangle(t)=\langle S_{3}\rangle(0)$ for every unit $\psi$, and applying the second part of [F5] to the assigned sharp observable $(S_{3},\mathrm{J\,s})$ of [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause (c) gives the time-independence of the law of $S_{3}$ in every preparation; moreover $S^{2}$ is a scalar operator by [F4] and commutes with $U_{Z}(t)$. This is (b) and the Casimir statement of (c). [step 1.1, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and the conjugation identities of (c), and step 2.2 proves (b) and the Casimir commutation of (c); only the uniform static profile, the componentwise free operator and the internal matrices were used, no inhomogeneous or time-dependent field, radiation, relaxation, apparatus or empirical input entered, which is the scope statement (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, F2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Sign and naming of the angular frequency.** The model's precession
  angular frequency is $\omega=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$, a signed quantity; the
  transverse vector rotates by $-\omega t$. Physical conventions differing by
  the sign of $\gamma_{s}$ or by the orientation of the field axis differ by
  the sign of $\omega$ and by the sense of the rotation, not by the content of
  the theorem.
- **Energy eigenvalues of the internal factor.** Combining this theorem with
  the spin spectrum page, the internal factor of the uniform-field model has
  the energy offsets $-\gamma_{s}B_{z}\hbar m$, $m=-s,\dots,s$, added to the
  free kinetic energy; the theorem does not assert a spectroscopic
  measurement or the absence of additional structure.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and of the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling, for a uniform static magnetic field along the third axis of a declared inertial frame: self-adjointness and factorization of the Zeeman energy operator, conservation of the spin component along the field, and Larmor precession of the transverse spin expectations with angular frequency gamma_s B_z. The item concerns the declared model only; it excludes inhomogeneous and time-dependent fields, radiation and relaxation, asserts no measured precession frequency or gyromagnetic ratio, and identifies no apparatus.

items.title: The conditional Stern-Gerlach force prediction of the spin-half Zeeman model: transverse momentum rate in a smooth bounded gradient field
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s=\tfrac12$, together with the effective
magnetic-moment coupling of
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] with parameter
$\gamma_{1/2}\in\mathbb R$ and the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$ be real with
$B_{z}$ and $B_{z}'$ bounded, let
$$\mathbf B(x):=\bigl(0,0,B_{z}(x_{1})\bigr),$$
let $H_{Z}$ be the Zeeman operator of the magnetic-moment postulate for this
profile, acting on $H_{1/2}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$ with domain
$D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$, and let $u(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}u_{0}$
be its flow. Identify $H_{1/2}$ with
$\mathcal H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\oplus L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
through the internal basis $(e_{1/2},e_{-1/2})$, and let $P_{+}:=\tfrac12(I+2S_{3}/\hbar)$
be the fibrewise orthogonal projection onto the spin-up line $e_{1/2}$.
Then:

(a) under this identification $H_{Z}$ is the operator
$$K(u_{+},u_{-})=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{+}-\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{+},\ \frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{-}+\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{-}\Bigr),\qquad D(K)=W^{2,2}\oplus W^{2,2},$$
of [[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conditional-stern-gerlach-force]] with
$\gamma_{s}:=\gamma_{1/2}$; consequently $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint,
$S_{3}H_{Z}=H_{Z}S_{3}$ on $D(H_{Z})$, the sector weights
$\|P_{\pm}u(t)\|^{2}$ and the mean $\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}$ are
independent of $t$;

(b) if in addition $u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$ is a unit vector with
$P_{+}u_{0}=u_{0}$ and $B_{z}'(x_{1})=G$ for every $x_{1}$ in a Borel set
$N\subseteq\mathbb R$ satisfying
$\int_{\mathbb R\setminus N}\eta_{+}(x_{1})\,dx_{1}=0$, where
$\eta_{+}(x_{1}):=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|u_{0}^{+}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}\,dx_{2}\,dx_{3}$
is the first-coordinate marginal density of the spin-up component, then
$$\frac{d}{dt}\Bigr|_{t=0}\bigl\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\bigr\rangle=\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}\,G ;$$
for $t\ne0$ the general rate is
$\frac{d}{dt}\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle=\gamma_{1/2}\langle S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u(t),u(t)\rangle$;

(c) the profile satisfies $\operatorname{div}\mathbf B=0$ and
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf B=(0,-B_{z}'(x_{1}),0)$ at every point of
$\mathbb R^{3}$, as identities of the displayed components;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
adopted coupling. Clause (b) is a model prediction for the rate of the mean
transverse momentum of a prepared spin-up state under the marginal-support
hypothesis; it is not an observation of a beam splitting, a trajectory or a
count, it identifies no apparatus, calibration or detector, and it asserts
neither a source-free realization of $\mathbf B$ nor a Maxwell solution.
The word "Stern-Gerlach" names this conditional model, not a reported
experiment; no measured value of $\gamma_{1/2}$ enters and no empirical
conclusion is drawn.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the magnetic-moment
postulate in the stated readings; the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of
Countable Choice; the model parameters $m>0$, $s=\tfrac12$,
$\gamma_{1/2}\in\mathbb R$; the field component $B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$
with $B_{z},B_{z}'$ bounded and the profile $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z}(x_{1}))$;
the operator $H_{Z}$ and the flow $u(t)$; a unit vector $u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$;
the real number $G$.

[F1] **Model operators.** On $H_{1/2}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$ the
componentwise operators $P_{j},Q_{j}$ and the internal operators
$S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ are those of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clauses (b),(c) and
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e); in the basis
$(e_{1/2},e_{-1/2})$ one has $S_{3}(u_{+},u_{-})=(\tfrac{\hbar}{2}u_{+},-\tfrac{\hbar}{2}u_{-})$
and $P_{+}=\tfrac12(I+2S_{3}/\hbar)$ projects fibrewise onto $e_{1/2}$.

[F2] **Zeeman operator of the model.** For the profile $\mathbf B$ with
bounded measurable components the Zeeman operator of
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] clause (ii) reads
$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{1/2}S_{3}B_{z}(Q_{x})$ on
$D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$, where $B_{z}(Q_{x})$ is
componentwise multiplication by $x\mapsto B_{z}(x_{1})$; it is self-adjoint
on that domain by the postulate's bounded-perturbation statement
([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

[F3] **The smooth bounded-coefficient force model.** With $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,
$\gamma_{s}\in\mathbb R$ and real $B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$ with $B_{z}$,
$B_{z}'$ bounded, the operator
$$K(u_{+},u_{-})=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{+}-\frac{\gamma_{s}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{+},\ \frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{-}+\frac{\gamma_{s}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{-}\Bigr),\quad D(K)=W^{2,2}\oplus W^{2,2},$$
on $\mathcal H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\oplus L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
is self-adjoint, $S_{z}K=KS_{z}$ on $D(K)$ for
$S_{z}(u_{+},u_{-})=(\tfrac{\hbar}{2}u_{+},-\tfrac{\hbar}{2}u_{-})$, the
sector weights and the mean of $S_{z}$ are conserved, for
$u_{0}\in D(K^{2})$ with $\|u_{0}\|=1$ the function
$t\mapsto\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle$ is $C^{1}$ with
$\frac{d}{dt}\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle=\gamma_{s}\langle S_{z}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u(t),u(t)\rangle$,
and if in addition $p_{+}u_{0}=u_{0}$ with $p_{\pm}:=\tfrac12(I\pm\frac{2}{\hbar}S_{z})$
and $B_{z}'=G$ on a Borel set carrying the first-coordinate marginal of
$u_{0}^{+}$, then
$\frac{d}{dt}|_{t=0}\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle=\frac{\gamma_{s}\hbar}{2}G$;
furthermore $\operatorname{div}\mathbf B=0$ and
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf B=(0,-B_{z}'(x_{1}),0)$ at every point
([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conditional-stern-gerlach-force]] clauses
(a),(b),(c),(d),
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]],
[[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the model's Zeeman operator with the
smooth bounded-coefficient force model through the internal basis, transport
the supplier's conservation, force and field identities, and read the
physical scope.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Identification of the operators] Under the identification of $H_{1/2}$ with $\mathcal H$ through $(e_{1/2},e_{-1/2})$, the model's componentwise operators $P_{j},Q_{j}$ of [F1] have exactly the componentwise form of the supplier's operators, whose self-adjointness and componentwise action are those of [F3]'s cited position-and-momentum items; the internal operator $S_{3}$ becomes the diagonal matrix with entries $\pm\hbar/2$, so $-\gamma_{1/2}S_{3}B_{z}(Q_{x})(u_{+},u_{-})=(-\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{+},+\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{-})$ and $H_{Z}=K$ with $\gamma_{s}:=\gamma_{1/2}$, including the domain $W^{2,2}\oplus W^{2,2}$; also $P_{\pm}=p_{\pm}$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Conservation and force] By step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{Z}=K$ is self-adjoint with $S_{3}H_{Z}=H_{Z}S_{3}$ on $D(H_{Z})$, so the sector weights $\|P_{\pm}u(t)\|^{2}$ and the mean $\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}$ are independent of $t$; for $u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$ with $P_{+}u_{0}=u_{0}$ and the marginal-support hypothesis, the supplier's identities give the general rate $\frac{d}{dt}\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle=\gamma_{1/2}\langle S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u(t),u(t)\rangle$ and the time-zero value $\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}G$, which are (a) and (b). [step 1.1, F3, algebra]

2.2 [Field identities] By [F3] the displayed profile satisfies $\operatorname{div}\mathbf B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\mathbf B=(0,-B_{z}'(x_{1}),0)$ at every point, which is (c). [step 1.1, F3]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 2.1 proves (a) and (b), and step 2.2 proves (c); only the displayed model operators, the adopted coupling and the supplier's conditional identities were used, no apparatus, trajectory, count, calibration or empirical value entered, which is the scope statement (d). [step 2.1, step 2.2, F2] ∎

## Remarks

- **What "force" means here.** Clause (b) is a rate of change of the mean of
  the transverse momentum operator in a declared preparation; it is the model
  counterpart of the classical force $-\nabla(-\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B)$
  and does not assert a classical trajectory or a definite transverse
  displacement of an individual particle.
- **The marginal hypothesis.** The support condition on
  $\eta_{+}$ is an explicit hypothesis on the preparation, not a general
  property of solutions; without it the general rate of clause (b) is the
  only identity available, since $B_{z}'$ enters pointwise.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and of the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling for the spin-half model in a static field profile B = (0,0,B_z(x_1)) whose component B_z is C^1 with bounded value and derivative: the identification of the model's Zeeman operator with the smooth bounded-coefficient force model, conservation of the field-aligned spin component and of the sector weights, the conditional rate gamma_s hbar G/2 of the transverse mean momentum in the spin-up sector when the gradient equals G on the support of the transverse marginal, and the divergence-free, curl identity of the profile. The item asserts no apparatus, no measured trajectory, no beam splitting observation and no source-free field realization; it is a model prediction conditional on its stated preparation assumptions.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 2 'Spin One-Half, Bras, Kets, and Operators', Section 1, printed pages 1-7 (the force on a magnetic dipole in a nonuniform magnetic field and the Stern-Gerlach two-peak idealization) and Section 4, printed pages 16-19 (spin states in an arbitrary direction)

items.title: Composition of two spin labels: total spin operators, the Clebsch-Gordan block decomposition and the spin-half singlet
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the composition postulate P1 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6 in the readings of
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] and
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix two declared
spin labels $s,t\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with internal factors
$V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$, $V_{t}=\mathbb C^{2t+1}$ and spin matrices
$J^{(s)}_{i}$, $J^{(t)}_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], and consider the
composite internal factor $V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ with the tensor-product
representation $D_{s}\otimes D_{t}$ assigned by P6 clause (ii). Put
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}:=\hbar\bigl(J^{(s)}_{i}\otimes I_{V_{t}}+I_{V_{s}}\otimes J^{(t)}_{i}\bigr),\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}:=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\bigl(S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\bigr)^{2},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}:=S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{3}.$$
Then:

(a) each $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ satisfying
$[S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{k}$,
$S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ is self-adjoint and commutes with every
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$, and
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=S^{(s)2}\otimes I_{V_{t}}+I_{V_{s}}\otimes S^{(t)2}+2\sum_{i=1}^{3}S^{(s)}_{i}\otimes S^{(t)}_{i};$$

(b) there is an orthogonal decomposition
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_{j}$ into
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}$-invariant subspaces with $\dim W_{j}=2j+1$, on each of
which the triple $(S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{1},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{2},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{3})$
is unitarily equivalent to the spin-$j$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] scaled by $\hbar$; in
particular $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=\hbar^{2}j(j+1)I$ on $W_{j}$, each $j$ occurs
exactly once, and there is an orthonormal basis $(v_{j,k})$,
$0\le k\le2j$, of $W_{j}$ with
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}v_{j,k}=\hbar(j-k)v_{j,k},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{+}v_{j,k}=\hbar\sqrt{k(2j-k+1)}\,v_{j,k-1},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{-}v_{j,k}=\hbar\sqrt{(k+1)(2j-k)}\,v_{j,k+1};$$
the coefficients of the $v_{j,k}$ in the product basis $(e^{(s)}_{m}\otimes e^{(t)}_{n})$
are the Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and are determined by the phase of the
top vector $u_{j}$ (a unit vector of $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-weight $\hbar j$
orthogonal to all $W_{j'}$ with $j'>j$), with $u_{s+t}=e^{(s)}_{s}\otimes e^{(t)}_{t}$
admissible;

(c) for every $M$ the $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-eigenspace with weight $\hbar M$
has dimension $N(M)=\#\{m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}:M-m\in\{-t,\dots,t\}\}$, and the
identity $(e^{(s)}_{m}\otimes e^{(t)}_{n})_{m,n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ of $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-eigenvectors with weights
$\hbar(m+n)$;

(d) for $s=t=\tfrac12$ one has $V_{1/2}\otimes V_{1/2}=W_{0}\oplus W_{1}$ with
$\dim W_{0}=1$ and $\dim W_{1}=3$; the vector
$$\Psi:=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(e^{(1/2)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(1/2)}_{-1/2}-e^{(1/2)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(1/2)}_{1/2}\bigr)$$
is a unit vector with $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for every $i$, and it is
the unique element of the kernel of $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ up to a phase;

(e) **Scope.** The statement concerns the internal factors of a declared
composite and the assignments of P1 and P6. It asserts no spatial
two-particle model, no statistics or permutation symmetry, no interaction, no
dynamics, no measurement and no empirical correlation; in particular it does
not by itself imply the singlet correlations of a separated pair, which
belong to the composites page.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1 and P6 in the stated readings; the Axiom of
Countable Choice; the spin labels $s,t$; the internal factors with their
bases $(e^{(s)}_{m})$, $(e^{(t)}_{n})$; the total spin operators; a real
number $M$.

[F1] **Finite spin matrices.** On $V_{s}$ the matrices $J^{(s)}_{i}$ are
self-adjoint with $[J^{(s)}_{i},J^{(s)}_{j}]=i\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}J^{(s)}_{k}$,
$J^{(s)2}=s(s+1)I$, $J^{(s)}_{+}e^{(s)}_{m}=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}e^{(s)}_{m+1}$
and $J^{(s)}_{z}e^{(s)}_{m}=me^{(s)}_{m}$ (and analogously for $t$)
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),(d)).

[F2] **Tensor spin composition.** On $V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ the operators
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}:=J^{(s)}_{i}\otimes I+I\otimes J^{(t)}_{i}$ are
self-adjoint with the angular momentum commutators,
$J^{\mathrm{tot}2}=J^{(s)2}\otimes I+I\otimes J^{(t)2}+2\sum_{i}J^{(s)}_{i}\otimes J^{(t)}_{i}$,
there is an orthogonal decomposition
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_{j}$ with $\dim W_{j}=2j+1$,
each $j$ occurring once, on each block the triple is unitarily equivalent to
the spin-$j$ matrices, the weight multiplicity is
$N(M)=\#\{m\in L_{s}:M-m\in L_{t}\}$ with the identity basis
$(e^{(s)}_{m}\otimes e^{(t)}_{n})$, and the block bases
$v_{j,k}=(k!(2j)\cdots(2j-k+1))^{-1/2}(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{-})^{k}u_{j}$
satisfy the displayed ladder actions, with the phase of $u_{j}$ fixing the
Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and $u_{s+t}=e^{(s)}_{s}\otimes e^{(t)}_{t}$
admissible
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]] clauses (a),(b),(c),(d),(e),
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[F3] **Internal-factor reading.** The composite internal factor $V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$
with the tensor-product representation is the assignment of P6 clause (ii)
for two declared spin labels under the composition postulate P1; the model's
spin observables are $S=\hbar J$ on each factor
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; rescale the matrix composition theorem by
$\hbar$, transfer its decomposition and ladder statements to the total spin
operators, and evaluate the spin-half singlet explicitly.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Operators and algebra] By [F2] the operators $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$ are self-adjoint with the angular momentum commutators and the displayed Casimir identity; multiplying by $\hbar$ and using $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}=\hbar J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$, $S^{(s)}_{i}=\hbar J^{(s)}_{i}$, $S^{(t)}_{i}=\hbar J^{(t)}_{i}$ and $S^{(s)2}=\hbar^{2}J^{(s)2}$ gives $[S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{k}$ and the identity of (a); $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ is self-adjoint as a sum of squares of commuting self-adjoint endomorphisms and commutes with each $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$ by [F2], which is (a). [F2, algebra]

1.2 [Singlet computation] Let $s=t=\tfrac12$ and $\Psi=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(e^{(s)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{-1/2}-e^{(s)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{1/2})$; by [F1] $J^{(s)}_{+}e^{(s)}_{1/2}=0$, $J^{(s)}_{+}e^{(s)}_{-1/2}=e^{(s)}_{1/2}$ and $J^{(s)}_{-}e^{(s)}_{1/2}=e^{(s)}_{-1/2}$, $J^{(s)}_{-}e^{(s)}_{-1/2}=0$, and analogously for $t$; hence $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{+}(e^{(s)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{-1/2})=e^{(s)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{1/2}=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{+}(e^{(s)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{1/2})$ and $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{-}(e^{(s)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{-1/2})=e^{(s)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{-1/2}=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{-}(e^{(s)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{1/2})$, so $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\pm}\Psi=0$ and therefore $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{1}\Psi=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{2}\Psi=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{3}\Psi=0$ by $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\pm}=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{1}\pm iJ^{\mathrm{tot}}_{2}$; $\Psi$ is unit because the product basis is orthonormal. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Decomposition and Clebsch-Gordan data] Transferring [F2] to the total spin operators by the rescaling of step 1.1 gives the orthogonal decomposition $V_{s}\otimes V_{t}=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_{j}$ with $\dim W_{j}=2j+1$, the unitary equivalence with the spin-$j$ matrices on each block and hence $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=\hbar^{2}j(j+1)I$ on $W_{j}$, the weight multiplicity of (c) and the identity basis; the block bases $v_{j,k}$ have the displayed ladder actions with the stated phase convention, which are (b) and (c). [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Uniqueness of the singlet] For $s=t=\tfrac12$ the decomposition of step 2.1 has the two blocks $j=0$ and $j=1$ with dimensions $1$ and $3$, and $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=0$ on the one-dimensional block $W_{0}$ and $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=\hbar^{2}\cdot2I$ on $W_{1}$; hence $\ker S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=W_{0}$ is one-dimensional, and since $\Psi\ne0$ satisfies $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}\Psi=0$ by step 1.2, it spans $W_{0}$: the kernel is the line $\mathbb C\Psi$. This is (d). [step 1.2, step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), step 2.1 proves (b),(c), and step 3.1 proves (d); only the internal factors, the assignments of [F3] and the finite matrix composition theorem were used, no spatial two-particle factor, statistics, dynamics, measurement or empirical input entered, which is the scope statement (e). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F3] ∎

## Remarks

- **Role of the page.** This theorem is the internal-factor supplier for the
  composites page, where the two-particle spatial factors, the preparation
  and the correlation analysis are added; no measured correlation or Bell
  statement is made here.
- **Phases.** The block vectors are determined by the phase of the top
  vector; different phases multiply all Clebsch-Gordan coefficients of a
  block by the same phase, so all outcome probabilities built from one block
  are unaffected.

The item concerns the internal factors only; the full two-particle spatial model, statistics, interactions and any measured correlation belong to the composites pages and are not asserted here.

items.statement:
## Scope and empirical status

- **Adopted assumptions.** This page adopts P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the
  readings of the framework and the spin assignment P6 of
  [[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)
  ([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
  [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). The
  effective magnetic-moment coupling with its gyromagnetic parameter
  $\gamma_{s}$ and bounded field profile is the additional model assumption
  [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]]; like the spin
  label, mass and charge, the parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is a species parameter
  with uncertainty and is not derived on this page.

- **What is proved.** The local mathematics
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] and
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] supplies the
  bounded-perturbation flow and the lifted SU(2) rotation action with its
  coordinate generators, and
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]] identifies the
  orbital Casimir on the harmonic blocks. On that basis:
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] gives the
  spectra and Born laws of the spin components;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-eigenstates-and-quantum-numbers]]
  describes the orbital eigenstates with the quantum numbers $l,m$ and the
  Casimir value; [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-total-conservation]] proves the
  conservation of the total angular momentum for a spin-independent
  rotation-invariant bounded-potential dynamics;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]] gives the Larmor
  precession of the transverse spin expectations and the conservation of the
  field component in a uniform static field;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] supplies the
  internal-factor composition with the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition and the
  spin-half singlet; and
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]] transfers
  the conditional smooth-field force identity to the model.

- **What is not claimed.** No result of this page derives any value of
  $\gamma_{s}$, $s$, $m$, $g$-factor or $\hbar$; no spin-orbit, fine or
  hyperfine structure, relativistic spinor, anomaly or radiative correction
  is included; no spin-statistics theorem is asserted; no atomic, molecular
  or solid-state model is constructed; and no statement about the
  compositeness or internal structure of any particle is made. The internal
  factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping device, not a rotating body.

- **Experiments.** This page contains no experiment item: it records no
  apparatus, calibration, sampling, count or uncertainty. The historical
  Stern-Gerlach setup appears only as the name of the conditional model of
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]], whose
  clause (b) is a prediction of the model conditional on an explicit
  preparation hypothesis. Identifying the operators and parameters of this
  page with a laboratory preparation and apparatus is a tested
  identification with uncertainty under
  [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; the measurement
  statistics of sequential spin filters are treated on the measurement pages
  of the category, and agreement or disagreement with data there constrains
  the combined model and apparatus assumptions without proving them.

- **Consumers.** Composites, Bell and identical-particle pages of the
  category consume the internal-factor results of
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] and the lifted rotation
  action of [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]];
  their empirical qualifications are added on those pages and are not
  inherited as certainty from this one.

items.title: Spin-half outcome probabilities along an arbitrary direction: the Bloch parametrization and worked cases
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, and the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Fix a unit vector
$f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and a unit internal spinor
$v=(v_{1},v_{2})\in\mathbb C^{2}$, and put
$$\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}:=\bigl(2\operatorname{Re}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}}),\ 2\operatorname{Im}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}}),\ |v_{1}|^{2}-|v_{2}|^{2}\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3}.$$
Let $\psi:=f\otimes v\in H_{1/2}$ and let $S_{n}=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$ be the
directional spin of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]]. Then:

(i) $\psi$ is a unit vector, $|\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}|=1$, and
for every unit $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$
$$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)=\frac{1+n\cdot\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}}{2},\qquad \mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{-\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)=\frac{1-n\cdot\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}}{2};$$

(ii) for the parametrization
$v=\bigl(e^{i\varphi}\cos(\theta/2),\ \sin(\theta/2)\bigr)$ with
$\theta\in[0,\pi]$ and $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ one has
$\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$,
and for the coordinate directions
$$\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)=\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2},\ \sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2},\qquad \mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)=\frac{1\pm\sin\theta\cos\varphi}{2};$$

(iii) for the basis state $v=e_{1/2}$ (the case $\theta=0$) the component
$S_{3}$ has the laws $\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})=1$ and
$\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=0$, while
$\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})=\tfrac12$ for both signs; and for
$v=(e_{1/2}+e_{-1/2})/\sqrt2$ the component $S_{1}$ has
$\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})=1$ and
$\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=0$.

All quantities are model probabilities for the pure preparation $[\psi]$; no
measurement procedure, apparatus, calibration or empirical frequency is
asserted, and the example makes no claim that a laboratory device realizes
the observable $S_{n}$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the stated readings; the
spin-half model with mass parameter $m>0$; the unit spatial factor $f$; the
unit internal spinor $v$; the vector $\psi=f\otimes v$; a unit direction
$n$; angles $\theta,\varphi$.

[F1] **Spin matrices of the model.** In the internal basis
$(e_{1/2},e_{-1/2})$ one has $S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ with the Pauli
matrices $\sigma_{1}=\sigma_{x}$, $\sigma_{2}=\sigma_{y}$,
$\sigma_{3}=\sigma_{z}$, and $S_{1}=S_{x}$, $S_{2}=S_{y}$, $S_{3}=S_{z}$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e),
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c),
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
clause (c)).

[F2] **Directional spectrum and law.** For every unit $n$ the operator
$S_{n}$ has the simple internal eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}$ with
eigenline projections $P_{\pm}=\tfrac12(I\pm n\cdot\sigma)$ read fibrewise,
and for every unit vector $\psi\in H_{1/2}$
$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\})=\langle P_{\pm}\psi,\psi\rangle$
([[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] clauses (a),(c),
[[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

[F3] **Preparations and the product form.** $\psi=f\otimes v$ is the
componentwise spinor $\psi(x)=f(x)v$ with $\|\psi\|=\|f\|\,\|v\|=1$, a unit
vector of the model's state space, hence a pure preparation
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (a),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the Pauli matrices on the spinor in the
product preparation and read the two projection weights.

**Given:** The data of the example and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Bloch vector] Writing $v=(v_{1},v_{2})$ with $|v_{1}|^{2}+|v_{2}|^{2}=1$, the inner products with the Pauli matrices computed from $\sigma_{1}v=(v_{2},v_{1})$, $\sigma_{2}v=(-iv_{2},iv_{1})$, $\sigma_{3}v=(v_{1},-v_{2})$ and the convention that the inner product is linear in the first argument give $\langle\sigma_{1}v,v\rangle=2\operatorname{Re}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}})$, $\langle\sigma_{2}v,v\rangle=2\operatorname{Im}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}})$ and $\langle\sigma_{3}v,v\rangle=|v_{1}|^{2}-|v_{2}|^{2}$, so $\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}$ is the vector of Pauli expectations, with $|\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}|^{2}=4|v_{1}v_{2}|^{2}+(|v_{1}|^{2}-|v_{2}|^{2})^{2}=(|v_{1}|^{2}+|v_{2}|^{2})^{2}=1$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 [Directional law] For the product vector $\psi=f\otimes v$ and a unit $n$, the fibrewise projection acts as $P_{\pm}\psi=f\otimes\tfrac12(I\pm n\cdot\sigma)v$, so by [F2], $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})=\tfrac12(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)v,v\rangle)=\tfrac12(1\pm n\cdot\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v})$ using step 1.1; this is (i). [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 [Parametrized spinor] For $v=(e^{i\varphi}\cos(\theta/2),\sin(\theta/2))$ one has $v_{1}\overline{v_{2}}=e^{i\varphi}\cos(\theta/2)\sin(\theta/2)$, so $2\operatorname{Re}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}})=\sin\theta\cos\varphi$, $2\operatorname{Im}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}})=\sin\theta\sin\varphi$ and $|v_{1}|^{2}-|v_{2}|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta/2)-\sin^{2}(\theta/2)=\cos\theta$; substituting $n=e_{3}$ and $n=e_{1}$ into step 2.1 gives the coordinate probabilities of (ii). [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Worked states] For $v=e_{1/2}$ the parametrization has $\theta=0$, so $\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}=(0,0,1)$ and step 2.1 gives $\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})=1$, $\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=0$ and $\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})=\tfrac12$; for $v=(e_{1/2}+e_{-1/2})/\sqrt2$ one has $\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}=(1,0,0)$ by step 1.1, and step 2.1 with $n=e_{1}$ gives $\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})=1$ and $\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=0$, which is (iii). [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **One preparation, all directions.** The Bloch vector determines the whole
  family of directional laws of this preparation; the example computes no
  joint law of two nonparallel directions, which is excluded by the
  incompatibility results of the uncertainty page.
- **No apparatus.** The probabilities are Born weights of the model; whether
  a given Stern-Gerlach or optical apparatus realizes $S_{n}$ is a tested
  identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not
  established here.
items.physical_scope: An exact computation inside the massive spin-half model of the framework: the Bloch parametrization of a unit internal spinor, the Born probabilities of the directional spin component n·S, and worked cases including the coordinate directions and the state e_{1/2}. The example uses the model's own outcome law; it involves no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus model, no measurement record and no empirical value.

items.title: Orbital angular momentum eigenfunctions: the low spherical harmonics of the massive model
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the mass parameter $m>0$, a spin label $s$ and the angular momentum
readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] for the
massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Y_{lm}$ be the spherical
harmonics of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] and
$h_{lm}$ their harmonic polynomial representatives of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]] clause (c), and
let $L_{i}$ be the orbital generators of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] with
$D_{i}=(x\times\nabla)_{i}$. Then:

(i) the harmonic polynomial representatives of the degrees $l=0$ and $l=1$
are
$$h_{00}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi}},\qquad h_{10}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4\pi}}\,x_{3},\qquad h_{1,1}=-\sqrt{\frac{3}{8\pi}}\,(x_{1}+ix_{2}),\qquad h_{1,-1}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{8\pi}}\,(x_{1}-ix_{2}),$$
and the family $(Y_{00},Y_{1,-1},Y_{10},Y_{11})$ is orthonormal in
$L^{2}(S^{2},\sigma)$;

(ii) on the degree-one block,
$$L_{3}h_{1m}=\hbar m\,h_{1m},\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=2\hbar^{2}F\quad(F\in V_{1}),$$
and on the degree-zero block $L_{i}Y_{00}=0$ for every $i$, so
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}Y_{00}=0$;

(iii) more generally, for every $l\ge0$ and $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$ the
statements $L_{3}Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$ and
$\sum_{i}\|L_{i}\varphi\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$ for the normalized angular
state $\varphi$ of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-eigenstates-and-quantum-numbers]] hold,
so the low-degree computations of (i),(ii) are the first two cases of that
theorem.

The example is a computation inside the angular theory; it involves no radial
function, no dynamics, no detector and no empirical input.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A mass parameter $m>0$ and a spin label $s$; the harmonic
polynomials $h_{lm}$ and the sphere functions $Y_{lm}$; the orbital
generators $L_{i}$ with $D_{i}=(x\times\nabla)_{i}$; the polar surface measure
$\sigma$ with $\sigma(S^{2})=4\pi$.

[F1] **Low harmonics.** The associated-polynomial normalization gives
$w_{00}=P_{0}=1$, $w_{10}=P_{1}=t$, $w_{11}=-(1-t^{2})^{1/2}$ with
$b_{00}=\bigl(\int_{-1}^{1}1\,dt\bigr)^{-1/2}=2^{-1/2}$,
$b_{10}=\bigl(\int_{-1}^{1}t^{2}dt\bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt{3/2}$ and
$b_{11}=\bigl(\int_{-1}^{1}(1-t^{2})dt\bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt{3/4}$, and the
polynomial representatives are $h_{00}=b_{00}/\sqrt{2\pi}$,
$h_{10}=b_{10}\,x_{3}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ and
$h_{1,\pm1}=\mp b_{11}(x_{1}\pm ix_{2})/\sqrt{2\pi}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] clauses
(c),(e), [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]]
clause (c)).

[F2] **Sphere integrals.** For the coordinate functions
$\Omega_{j}(x)=x_{j}/|x|$ one has $\int_{S^{2}}\Omega_{i}\Omega_{j}\,d\sigma=\frac{4\pi}{3}\delta_{ij}$
and $\int_{S^{2}}1\,d\sigma=4\pi$, computed in angle coordinates
$\Phi(\theta,\varphi)$ with $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$
([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]],
[[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]],
[[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]],
[[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]]).

[F3] **Core action and Casimir on blocks.** For polynomial representatives
one has $L_{i}F=\mathrm{res}_{l}(-i\hbar D_{i}p_{F})$ and
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ for $F\in V_{l}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] clause (a),
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F4] **General eigenstate theorem.** For every $l,m$ and every radial profile
$R\in C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty))$ the model vector $R(|x|)h_{lm}(x)w$ has
$L_{3}$-eigenvalue $\hbar m$ and Casimir form value $\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$
([[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-eigenstates-and-quantum-numbers]]
clauses (a),(b),(c)).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; insert the explicit low-degree polynomials, evaluate the sphere integrals in angle coordinates, and apply the polynomial action of the generators and the Casimir identity on the degree-one block.

**Given:** The data of the example and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Low polynomials] Substituting the constants of [F1] gives $h_{00}=2^{-1/2}(2\pi)^{-1/2}=(4\pi)^{-1/2}$, $h_{10}=\sqrt{3/2}(2\pi)^{-1/2}x_{3}=\sqrt{3/(4\pi)}x_{3}$, and $h_{1,\pm1}=\mp\sqrt{3/4}(2\pi)^{-1/2}(x_{1}\pm ix_{2})=\mp\sqrt{3/(8\pi)}(x_{1}\pm ix_{2})$, which are the displayed polynomials of (i); each is harmonic and homogeneous of the stated degree by [F1]. [F1, algebra]

2.1 [Sphere norms and orthogonality] By [F2] and step 1.1, $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{00}|^{2}d\sigma=\frac{1}{4\pi}\cdot4\pi=1$; $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{10}|^{2}d\sigma=\frac{3}{4\pi}\int\Omega_{3}^{2}d\sigma=\frac{3}{4\pi}\cdot\frac{4\pi}{3}=1$; and $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{1,\pm1}|^{2}d\sigma=\frac{3}{8\pi}\int(\Omega_{1}^{2}+\Omega_{2}^{2})d\sigma=\frac{3}{8\pi}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}=1$; the mixed integrals vanish because every integrand contains an odd power of one coordinate, whose $\varphi$-integral over $(0,2\pi)$ vanishes by the primitive of sine and cosine; hence the four functions are orthonormal. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Degree-one eigenvalues] By step 1.1 and [F3], $D_{3}h_{1m}=(x_{1}\partial_{2}-x_{2}\partial_{1})h_{1m}=im\,h_{1m}$ for $m=-1,0,1$ (checked on the explicit monomials), hence $L_{3}h_{1m}=\hbar mh_{1m}$, and the Casimir identity of [F3] with $l=1$ gives $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=2\hbar^{2}F$ for $F\in V_{1}$; for $F=Y_{00}$ the same identity with $l=0$ gives $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}Y_{00}=0$, and since the $L_{i}$ are self-adjoint and commute with $L^{2}$-norms this forces $L_{i}Y_{00}=0$ because $\sum_{i}\|L_{i}Y_{00}\|^{2}=0$, which is (ii). [step 1.1, F3, algebra]

3.1 [General case] Clause (iii) restates [F4] in the normalization $\|Y_{lm}\|=1$; combining it with step 2.2 gives the low-degree instances, completing the verification of (i)-(iii). [step 2.1, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **The $l=0$ exception.** The vanishing of all three components on $Y_{00}$
  illustrates that a state with zero total orbital angular momentum has every
  component sharp at value zero; the noncommutation of two components on
  other states is not contradicted.
- **No radial statement.** The example uses only angular representatives; the
  radial factor of a physical state, its normalization and its dynamics
  belong to the radial and Coulomb pages.

The example concerns the spatial angular factor; it asserts no dynamics, no radial spectrum, no measurement and no empirical value.
