items.title: The two-level Zeeman toy model: sector energies, level splitting and spin precession
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, together with the effective magnetic-moment coupling of
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] with parameter
$\gamma:=\gamma_{1/2}\in\mathbb R$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and the uniform field
$\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z})$, let
$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma B_{z}S_{3}$ on $D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$
be the model's Zeeman operator with flow $U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$ and put
$\omega:=\gamma B_{z}$. Then:

(i) for every unit $f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and each sign,
$$H_{Z}\bigl(f\otimes e_{\pm}\bigr)=\bigl(H_{0}f\bigr)\otimes e_{\pm}\mp\frac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2}\,f\otimes e_{\pm},\qquad \bigl\langle H_{Z}\bigr\rangle_{f\otimes e_{\pm}}=\bigl\langle H_{0}\bigr\rangle_{f}\mp\frac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2},$$
and for the product flow
$U_{Z}(t)\bigl(f\otimes e_{\pm}\bigr)=e^{\mp i\gamma B_{z}t/2}\bigl(e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}f\bigr)\otimes e_{\pm}$;
the transverse spin means of such a product state precess as in
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]];

(ii) **toy truncation.** Suppose in addition that, on a declared
two-dimensional internal subspace, the free part is replaced by the scalar
$E_{0}I$ (a truncation assumption of the toy model, not a theorem of the full
model): then the truncated operator is
$H_{Z}^{(2)}=E_{0}I-\gamma B_{z}S_{3}=\bigl(E_{0}-\tfrac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2}\bigr)e_{+}e_{+}^{*}+\bigl(E_{0}+\tfrac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2}\bigr)e_{-}e_{-}^{*}$
in the basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$, with energy levels
$E_{0}\mp\tfrac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2}$ and signed level difference
$\Delta E:=\gamma\hbar B_{z}=\hbar\omega$; its evolution is
$$e^{-itH_{Z}^{(2)}/\hbar}=e^{-itE_{0}/\hbar}\begin{pmatrix}e^{i\omega t/2}&0\\0&e^{-i\omega t/2}\end{pmatrix},$$
so the relative phase of the two amplitudes accumulates at the angular
frequency $\omega$ (equivalently at the ordinary frequency
$|\omega|/(2\pi)$);

(iii) in the truncation the conjugation identities of the precession theorem
reduce to explicit matrix identities,
$$V(t)^{*}\sigma_{1}V(t)=\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{1}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{2},\qquad V(t)^{*}\sigma_{2}V(t)=\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{2}-\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{1},$$
with $V(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}^{(2)}/\hbar}e^{itE_{0}/\hbar}$;

(iv) the toy model contains no driving field: it predicts a stationary
relative phase, hence no spin flip between $e_{+}$ and $e_{-}$ under
$H_{Z}^{(2)}$ alone. Statements about spin-flip transitions, resonance or
spectroscopy require a separately adopted drive or coupling, belong to the
driven-dynamics and light-matter pages, and are not derived here. No
apparatus, calibration, measured frequency or measured value of $\gamma$ is
asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the magnetic-moment
postulate in the stated readings; the two choice principles; the parameters
$m>0$, $s=\tfrac12$, $\gamma\in\mathbb R$, $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and
$\omega=\gamma B_{z}$; the operator $H_{Z}$ and its flow; a unit
$f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$; the basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$; the scalar
$E_{0}$.

[F1] **Uniform-field Zeeman operator.** $H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma B_{z}S_{3}$ is
self-adjoint on $D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$ with flow
$U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}e^{it\gamma B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}$, $S_{3}$ commutes
with the flow, and for every unit vector the transverse means satisfy the
precession identities of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]] clauses (a),(b),(c)
([[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] clauses (i),(ii),
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

[F2] **Spin-half matrices.** $S_{3}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{3}$ with
$\sigma_{3}e_{\pm}=\pm e_{\pm}$, $S_{1}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{1}$,
$S_{2}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{2}$, and the Pauli matrices satisfy
$\sigma_{1}^{2}=\sigma_{2}^{2}=I$, $\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}=i\sigma_{3}$,
$\sigma_{2}\sigma_{1}=-i\sigma_{3}$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e),
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
clause (c)).

[F3] **Bounded exponentials.** For a bounded self-adjoint matrix $A$ the
map $t\mapsto e^{-itA/\hbar}=\sum_{n}(-itA/\hbar)^{n}/n!$ is a norm-continuous
unitary group with $(e^{-itA/\hbar})^{*}=e^{itA/\hbar}$
([[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]],
[[def-operator-norm]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the Zeeman operator on the product basis of sectors, read the eigenvalues of the truncated internal matrix, and compute the conjugated Pauli matrices explicitly.

**Given:** The data of the example and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Sector identities] By [F2] one has $S_{3}(f\otimes e_{\pm})=\pm\frac{\hbar}{2}f\otimes e_{\pm}$ and $H_{0}$ acts on the spatial factor only, so $H_{Z}(f\otimes e_{\pm})=(H_{0}f)\otimes e_{\pm}\mp\frac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2}f\otimes e_{\pm}$; taking the inner product with $f\otimes e_{\pm}$ (a unit vector for unit $f$) gives the displayed expectation; by [F1] the flow factors, so $U_{Z}(t)(f\otimes e_{\pm})=e^{\mp i\gamma B_{z}t/2}(e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}f)\otimes e_{\pm}$, and the precession statements of the transverse means are those of the cited theorem, which is (i). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Toy levels and evolution] In the two-dimensional internal model with free part $E_{0}I$, the operator $H_{Z}^{(2)}=E_{0}I-\gamma B_{z}S_{3}$ is diagonal in $(e_{+},e_{-})$ with entries $E_{0}\mp\frac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2}$ by [F2], so its eigenvalues are those entries and the signed difference is $\gamma\hbar B_{z}=\hbar\omega$; by [F3] the exponential is the displayed diagonal unitary, and the relative phase accumulates at the angular frequency $\omega$, which is (ii). [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 [Conjugation identities] With $V(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}^{(2)}/\hbar}e^{itE_{0}/\hbar}=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\omega t/2},e^{-i\omega t/2})$ from step 2.1, direct matrix multiplication using [F2] gives $V(t)^{*}\sigma_{1}V(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&e^{-i\omega t}\\ e^{i\omega t}&0\end{pmatrix}=\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{1}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{2}$ and $V(t)^{*}\sigma_{2}V(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-ie^{-i\omega t}\\ ie^{i\omega t}&0\end{pmatrix}=\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{2}-\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{1}$, which is (iii) and agrees with the general conjugation of [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]] clause (c). [step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 [Scope] Since $H_{Z}^{(2)}$ is diagonal in $(e_{+},e_{-})$, its evolution multiplies the two amplitudes by phases and preserves the sector weights $|c_{\pm}|^{2}$: no spin flip occurs without a driving term, and the truncation was an explicit toy assumption, which is (iv). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the truncation discards.** Replacing $H_{0}$ by $E_{0}I$ discards the
  kinetic and any potential structure of the spatial factor; the truncated
  model is a toy description of the internal degree of freedom, and no
  spatial dynamics or position-space measurement model follows from it.
- **Frequency conventions.** $\omega=\gamma B_{z}$ is an angular frequency in
  $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; the ordinary frequency is $|\omega|/(2\pi)$ in hertz,
  with the radian dimensionless, in the conventions of
  [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].
items.physical_scope: A worked example inside the massive spin-half model with the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling in a uniform static field: the exact sector identities for the Zeeman operator on product states, the energy offsets, and an explicitly labeled two-level truncation in which the internal levels differ by gamma hbar B_z and the spin precesses with angular frequency gamma B_z. The truncation is a toy model assumption, not derived from the full operator; no spectroscopy, no radiation, no measured gyromagnetic parameter and no apparatus is asserted.

items.title: The idealized Stern-Gerlach splitting: transverse momentum separation of the two spin sectors under a window hypothesis
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the effective magnetic-moment
coupling as in
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]], for the
massive spin-$\tfrac12$ model with mass parameter $m>0$ and parameter
$\gamma:=\gamma_{1/2}\in\mathbb R$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]]), and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a real
$B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$ with $B_{z}$, $B_{z}'$ bounded, reals $0<a<\infty$
and $G$, and the field profile $\mathbf B(x)=(0,0,B_{z}(x_{1}))$, and
**suppose** that $B_{z}'(x_{1})=G$ for every $x_{1}\in(-a,a)$. Let
$H_{Z}$ be the Zeeman operator of the model with flow
$u(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}u_{0}$ for a unit vector
$u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$, let
$u_{\pm}(t):=P_{\pm}u(t)$ be the two spin-sector components with
$P_{\pm}=\tfrac12(I\pm 2S_{3}/\hbar)$, and write
$w_{\pm}:=\|u_{\pm}(0)\|^{2}$ and, for each sign, let
$$\eta_{\pm}(t,x_{1}):=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}\bigl|u_{\pm}^{\pm}(t,x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\bigr|^{2}\,dx_{2}\,dx_{3}$$
be the first-coordinate marginal density of the $\pm$ component of
$u_{\pm}(t)$, where $u_{\pm}^{\pm}$ denotes that nonzero component. Fix
$\tau>0$ and adopt the following **hypothetical containment premise**: for
each sign and every $t\in[0,\tau]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R\setminus(-a,a)}\eta_{\pm}(t,x_{1})\,dx_{1}=0 .$$
Then:

(i) the sector weights are conserved: $\|u_{\pm}(t)\|^{2}=w_{\pm}$ for every
$t$, and $\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}(w_{+}-w_{-})$ is
independent of $t$;

(ii) under the containment premise, for each sign with $w_{\pm}>0$ the
normalized sector transverse mean
$M_{\pm}(t):=w_{\pm}^{-1}\langle P_{x}u_{\pm}(t),u_{\pm}(t)\rangle$ is affine
in $t$ on $[0,\tau]$:
$$\frac{d}{dt}M_{\pm}(t)=\pm\frac{\gamma\hbar G}{2},\qquad M_{\pm}(\tau)=M_{\pm}(0)\pm\frac{\gamma\hbar G\tau}{2},$$
so the two sector mean transverse momenta (both defined when $w_{+}w_{-}>0$)
differ by $\gamma\hbar G\tau$ at time $\tau$, independently of the initial
means; a sector with $w_{\pm}=0$ is trivial;

(iii) the total transverse mean evolves by the weighted rate
$$\frac{d}{dt}\bigl\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\bigr\rangle =\frac{\gamma\hbar G}{2}(w_{+}-w_{-})=\gamma G\,\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u_{0}}, \qquad t\in[0,\tau],$$
so for the equal-weight preparation $w_{+}=w_{-}=\tfrac12$ the total
transverse mean is conserved while the sector means separate;

(iv) **Status and scope.** This is an idealized hypothetical calculation: the
containment premise is an explicitly assumed possible property of the
evolved state, not an observed fact and not a consequence of the model; no
position-space splitting, detector trace, count, calibration or measured
value is asserted, no apparatus is modeled, and the historical
Stern-Gerlach experiment is not described or explained by this item. The
identification of the model with any real beam experiment remains a tested
identification with uncertainty under
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the magnetic-moment
postulate in the stated readings; the two choice principles; the parameters
$m>0$, $s=\tfrac12$, $\gamma\in\mathbb R$ and the real
$B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$ with $B_{z},B_{z}'$ bounded; the reals $a>0$,
$G$, $\tau>0$; the profile $\mathbf B$; the operator $H_{Z}$; the flow
$u(t)$; the unit vector $u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$; the sector projections
$P_{\pm}$; the marginal densities $\eta_{\pm}$.

[F1] **Model force theorem.** For the present model and profile, with the
identifications of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]] clauses
(a),(b): $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint on $W^{2,2}$, $S_{3}$ commutes with $H_{Z}$
on the domain, the sector weights $\|P_{\pm}u(t)\|^{2}$ and the mean
$\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}$ are independent of $t$, and for every
$v_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$ with flow $v(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}v_{0}$ one has
$$\frac{d}{dt}\bigl\langle P_{x}v(t),v(t)\bigr\rangle =\gamma\,\bigl\langle S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})v(t),v(t)\bigr\rangle ;$$
if additionally $P_{+}v_{0}=v_{0}$ and $B_{z}'=G$ on a Borel set carrying the
first-coordinate marginal of $v_{0}^{+}$, then
$\frac{d}{dt}|_{t=0}\langle P_{x}v(t),v(t)\rangle=\frac{\gamma\hbar}{2}G$; in
the model readings the operator $S_{3}$ is
$\tfrac{\hbar}{2}$ times the Pauli $\sigma_{z}$ on the internal factor
([[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]] clauses
(a),(b), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e),
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
clause (c)).

[F2] **Sector invariance.** $P_{\pm}=\tfrac12(I\pm 2S_{3}/\hbar)$ are
orthogonal projections with $P_{+}+P_{-}=I$ and
$S_{3}P_{\pm}=\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}P_{\pm}$; since $S_{3}$ commutes with
$H_{Z}$ on $D(H_{Z})$ by [F1], $P_{\pm}$ commute with $H_{Z}$, preserve
$D(H_{Z})$ and $D(H_{Z}^{2})$, and commute with the flow, so
$u_{\pm}(t)=P_{\pm}u(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}P_{\pm}u_{0}$ lies in the $\pm$
spin sector for every $t$, with $\|u_{\pm}(t)\|=w_{\pm}^{1/2}$
([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

[F3] **Hypothetical containment premise.** It is assumed that for each sign
and every $t\in[0,\tau]$ the density $\eta_{\pm}(t,\cdot)$ is supported in
$(-a,a)$; under this premise, since $B_{z}'(x_{1})=G$ for $x_{1}\in(-a,a)$ by
the window hypothesis, the identity $S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u_{\pm}(t)
=\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}G\,u_{\pm}(t)$ holds as classes. This premise is assumed,
not derived, and is labeled hypothetical
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; decompose the state into the conserved spin
sectors, apply the conditional force identity to each sector with the window
premise, and integrate the resulting constant rates.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Sector decomposition and conservation] By [F2] the sector components $u_{\pm}(t)$ satisfy $u_{\pm}(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}u_{\pm}(0)$ with $u_{\pm}(0)=P_{\pm}u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$, $\|u_{\pm}(t)\|^{2}=w_{\pm}$, and $\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\|u_{+}(t)\|^{2}-\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\|u_{-}(t)\|^{2}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}(w_{+}-w_{-})$ is independent of $t$; this is (i). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Sector rates] Apply the general rate identity of [F1] to each sector component $u_{\pm}$: $\frac{d}{dt}\langle P_{x}u_{\pm}(t),u_{\pm}(t)\rangle=\gamma\langle S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u_{\pm}(t),u_{\pm}(t)\rangle$; by the numerical identity $S_{3}u_{\pm}(t)=\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}u_{\pm}(t)$ of [F2] and the premise [F3] giving $S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u_{\pm}(t)=\pm\frac{\hbar}{2}Gu_{\pm}(t)$, the right-hand side equals $\pm\frac{\gamma\hbar G}{2}\|u_{\pm}(t)\|^{2}=\pm\frac{\gamma\hbar G}{2}w_{\pm}$; dividing by the constant sector weight $w_{\pm}>0$ gives $\frac{d}{dt}M_{\pm}(t)=\pm\frac{\gamma\hbar G}{2}$ on $[0,\tau]$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 [Integration and separation] Integrating the constant rates of step 2.1 over $[0,\tau]$ gives $\langle P_{x}u_{\pm}(\tau),u_{\pm}(\tau)\rangle=\langle P_{x}u_{\pm}(0),u_{\pm}(0)\rangle\pm\frac{\gamma\hbar G\tau}{2}$ for the normalized sector means; subtracting the two identities gives the separation $\gamma\hbar G\tau$ of the sector means, and adding them with the weights $w_{\pm}$ and using $u(t)=u_{+}(t)+u_{-}(t)$ with orthogonality of the sectors gives $\frac{d}{dt}\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle=\frac{\gamma\hbar G}{2}(w_{+}-w_{-})=\gamma G\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u_{0}}$ and the conservation of the total mean for $w_{+}=w_{-}$, which are (ii) and (iii). [step 2.1, step 1.1, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 prove (i)-(iii) under the explicit premise [F3]; the premise is hypothetical, no position-space trace, count or apparatus entered, and no empirical conclusion is drawn, which is the status statement (iv). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F3] ∎

## Remarks

- **Normalization of the means.** The mean transverse momentum of a sector is
  read from the outcome law of the whole preparation restricted to the
  sector, that is from the normalized sector mean; the statement and the
  proof use this reading, and the sector rate is constant under the window
  premise.
- **How strong the premise is.** The containment premise constrains the
  prepared state and the field window jointly; for a spreading wave packet
  and a finite window it can fail for large $\tau$ or narrow packets, and the
  item asserts nothing about when it holds. The physical two-beam profile of
  a real Stern-Gerlach magnet is not modeled here.
items.physical_scope: An idealized model prediction of the spin-half Zeeman model with a static windowed-gradient field: under an explicitly hypothetical containment premise (the first-coordinate marginals of both spin-sector components remain supported in the window of constant gradient during [0,tau]), the sector mean transverse momenta separate at the rate gamma hbar G / 2 and by gamma hbar G tau over the time tau, while the sector weights and the total transverse mean are conserved. The item is a hypothetical calculation, not a reported experiment: it asserts no apparatus, no beam, no counts, no detector, no measured value and no claim that the containment premise holds for realistic preparations.

items.title: What the angular momentum examples establish and what they do not
items.statement:
## Scope of the examples

- **Recorded content.** The companion page contains exact model computations:
  [[ex-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-half-directional-probabilities]] evaluates
  the Born probabilities of the directional spin components for an arbitrary
  unit spinor and works the coordinate cases;
  [[ex-nrqm-angular-momentum-l-eigenfunctions]] computes the low spherical
  harmonics, their orthonormality and their orbital eigenvalues;
  [[ex-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-toy-model]] records the sector expressions
  of the uniform-field Zeeman operator, an explicitly labeled two-level
  truncation with its level splitting, and the explicit precession matrices;
  and [[texp-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-splitting]] derives, under an
  explicitly hypothetical containment premise, the separation of the two
  sector mean transverse momenta.

- **Status.** All four items are conditional statements inside the model of
  [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with the readings of
  [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and, in
  the last two, with the adopted magnetic-moment coupling. None of them
  reports a measurement; the thought experiment's containment premise is a
  hypothetical assumption, and the toy truncation is a toy model assumption;
  the numerical values appearing in them ($\hbar$-multiples, probabilities
  and frequencies) are model expressions, not measured numbers.

- **Empirical qualifications.** The identification of any of these
  preparations and observables with a laboratory setup is a tested
  identification with uncertainty under
  [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; detector resolution,
  background, calibration, sampling and selection are not modeled here. The
  item [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]] and
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] supply the
  general laws the examples specialize, and their qualifications carry over
  to every example.

- **What is deliberately absent.** No experiment item, no measured
  frequency, no measured gyromagnetic parameter, no source-backed
  Stern-Gerlach dataset, no spin-orbit or fine-structure computation and no
  radiation or relaxation model appears on the examples companion; those
  belong to other pages of the category, with their own sources and
  qualifications.
